title.zh: 卷一百四十二 志第九十五 樂十七
title.raw: 卷一百四十二 志第九十五 樂十七 Volume 142 Treatises 95: Music 17

sentences.zh: 樂十七○詩樂琴律燕樂教坊雲韶部鈞容直四夷樂

translations.literal: Music 17 ○ Poetry Music, Qin Pitch Standards, Yan Music, Music Office, Cloud Sho Music Bureau, Junrong Direct [ensemble], Four Barbarians' Music
translations.idiomatic: Music 17 — Poetry Music; Qin Pitch Standards; Yan Music; the Teaching Office; the Cloud Sho Music Bureau; the Junrong Direct; Music of the Four Barbarians

sentences.zh: 詩樂虞庭言樂，以詩為本。

translations.literal: In poetry music, the court of Yu and Shun spoke of music with the Odes as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tradition of poetry music, the court of Yu and Shun held that music takes the Odes as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 孔門禮樂之教，自興於《詩》始。

translations.literal: The Confucian teaching of ritual and music began to flourish starting from the Book of Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian instruction in ritual and music first arose with the Book of Odes.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：“十有三年學樂、誦詩。

translations.literal: The Record states: "At thirteen one studies music and recites the Odes."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "At thirteen one studies music and recites the Odes."

sentences.zh: ”詠歌以養其性情，舞蹈以養其血脈，此古之成材所以為易也。

translations.literal: "Singing the odes nurtures one's nature and disposition; dancing nurtures one's blood and pulse — this is why molding accomplished persons in antiquity was easy."
translations.idiomatic: "Singing the odes cultivates character; dancing invigorates the body — which is why training accomplished persons was so straightforward in ancient times."

sentences.zh: 宋朝湖學之興，老師宿儒痛正音之寂寥，嚐擇取《二南》、《小雅》數十篇，寓之塤籥，使學者朝夕詠歌。

translations.literal: When the Lake Academy of the Song rose, veteran masters grieved the desolation of orthodox tones; they once selected dozens of pieces from the Two Souths and the Minor Odes, setting them to xun and yue pipes so that students might sing them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lake Academy flourished in the Song, senior masters lamented how orthodox tones had fallen silent; they selected dozens of pieces from the Two Souths and the Minor Odes, set them for xun and yue pipes, and had students sing them morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 自爾聲詩之學，為儒者稍知所尚。

translations.literal: From then on, the study of tonal poetry became something Confucian scholars slightly knew to esteem.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, the study of sung poetry came to be something Confucian scholars at least knew to value.

sentences.zh: 張載嚐慨然思欲講明，作之朝廷，被諸郊廟矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai once pondered earnestly how to expound this clearly, present it at court, and extend it to the suburban altars and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai once resolved in earnest to expound this practice, introduce it at court, and extend it to the suburban altars and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 朱熹述為詩篇，彙於學禮，將使後之學者學焉。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi compiled them into poetry pieces gathered in the Study of Ritual, intending that later learners should study them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi set them out as sung poems and collected them in the Study of Ritual, so that later students might learn them.

sentences.zh: 《小雅》歌凡六篇：

translations.literal: Minor Odes songs total six pieces:
translations.idiomatic: Songs from the Minor Odes number six in all:

sentences.zh: 朱熹曰：“《傳》曰：‘大學始教，宵雅肄三。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said: "The Commentary states: 'At the beginning of university instruction, the xiao ya are practiced three times.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said: "The Commentary states: 'At the beginning of university instruction, students practice the xiao ya three times.'"

sentences.zh: ’謂習《小雅·鹿鳴》、《四牡》、《皇皇者華》之三詩也。

translations.literal: 'This means practicing the three odes Deer Cry, Four Steeds, and Splendid Are the Flowers.'
translations.idiomatic: This refers to practicing the three Minor Odes "Deer Cry," "Four Steeds," and "Splendid Are the Flowers."

sentences.zh: 此皆君臣宴勞之詩，始學者習之，所以取其上下相和厚也。

translations.literal: These are all odes for feasting and rewarding between ruler and ministers; beginning students practice them in order to take their message of mutual harmony and warmth between superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: These are all odes for banquets and rewards between ruler and ministers; beginning students learn them to absorb their lesson of harmony and mutual regard between superior and inferior.

sentences.zh: 古鄉飲酒及燕禮皆歌此三詩。

translations.literal: In antiquity, both the district drinking ceremony and the banquet rite sang these three odes.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, both the district drinking ceremony and the banquet rite featured these three odes.

sentences.zh: 及笙入，六笙間歌《魚麗》、《南有嘉魚》、《南山有台》。

translations.literal: When the sheng entered, the six sheng alternately sang Fish Abundant, Southward the Fine Fish, and South Mountain Has Its Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When the sheng entered, the six sheng players alternately sang "Fish Abundant," "Southward the Fine Fish," and "South Mountain Has Its Terrace."

sentences.zh: 六笙詩本無辭，其遺聲亦不復傳矣。

translations.literal: The six sheng odes originally had no texts, and their surviving sounds are no longer transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The six sheng pieces originally had no texts, and their surviving melodies are no longer handed down.

sentences.zh: 《小雅》為諸侯之樂，《大雅》、《頌》為天子之樂。

translations.literal: The Minor Odes are music for feudal lords; the Major Odes and the Hymns are music for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Minor Odes are music for feudal lords; the Major Odes and the Hymns are music for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二南《國風》歌凡六篇：

translations.literal: Songs from the Two Souths of the Airs of the States total six pieces:
translations.idiomatic: Songs from the Two Souths in the Airs of the States number six in all:

sentences.zh: 朱熹曰：“‘《周南》、《召南》，正始之道，王化之基。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said: "'The Zhou South and the Shao South are the way of the correct beginning and the foundation of royal transformation.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said: "'The Zhou South and the Shao South embody the way of the correct beginning and form the foundation of royal civilizing influence.'"

sentences.zh: ’‘故用之鄉人焉，用之邦國焉。

translations.literal: 'Therefore they are used among the people of the district and used among the states of the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they are used among the people of the district and used among the states of the realm.

sentences.zh: ’《鄉飲酒》及《鄉射禮》：‘合樂，《周南》：《關雎》、《葛覃》、《卷耳》；

translations.literal: 'The District Drinking Rite and the District Archery Rite state: "Combined music — Zhou South: Ospreys, Kudzu Vine, and Ears of Wolf's-tail."'
translations.idiomatic: The District Drinking Rite and the District Archery Rite state: "For combined music — from the Zhou South: 'Ospreys,' 'Kudzu Vine,' and 'Ears of Wolf's-tail';"

sentences.zh: 《召南》：《鵲巢》、《采蘩》、《采蘋》。

translations.literal: Shao South: Magpie's Nest, Gathering White Artemisia, and Gathering Duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: from the Shao South: 'Magpie's Nest,' 'Gathering White Artemisia,' and 'Gathering Duckweed.'

sentences.zh: ’《燕禮》云：‘遂歌鄉樂。

translations.literal: 'The Banquet Rite says: "Then they sing the district music."'
translations.idiomatic: The Banquet Rite says: "Then they sing the district music."

sentences.zh: ’即此六篇也。

translations.literal: 'These are precisely these six pieces.'
translations.idiomatic: These are precisely the six pieces in question.

sentences.zh: 合樂，謂歌舞與眾聲皆作。

translations.literal: Combined music means that song, dance, and all the ensemble sounds are performed together.
translations.idiomatic: Combined music means that singing, dancing, and all ensemble sounds are performed together.

sentences.zh: 《周南》、《召南》，古房中之樂歌也。

translations.literal: The Zhou South and the Shao South are ancient chamber music songs.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou South and the Shao South are ancient songs of the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 《關雎》言後妃之誌，《鵲巢》言國君夫人之德，《采蘩》言夫人之不失職，《采蘋》言卿大夫妻能循法度。

translations.literal: Ospreys speaks of the aspirations of the queen consort; Magpie's Nest speaks of the virtue of the ruler's wife; Gathering White Artemisia speaks of the wife not failing in her duties; Gathering Duckweed speaks of the wife of a high minister and grandee being able to follow the standards of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: "Ospreys" treats the aspirations of the queen consort; "Magpie's Nest" treats the virtue of the ruler's wife; "Gathering White Artemisia" treats a wife who does not fail in her duties; "Gathering Duckweed" treats the wife of a high minister who can follow the standards of propriety.

sentences.zh: 夫婦之道，生民之本，王化之端，此六篇者，其教之原也。

translations.literal: The way of husband and wife is the root of the people and the beginning of royal transformation; these six pieces are the origin of that teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The way of husband and wife is the foundation of the people and the starting point of royal civilizing influence; these six pieces are the source of that teaching.

sentences.zh: 故國君與其臣下及四方之賓燕，用之合樂也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the ruler of a state feasts with his ministers and guests from the four quarters, these are used in combined music.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a state's ruler feasts with his ministers and guests from the four quarters, these pieces are performed as combined music.

sentences.zh: 《小雅》詩譜：《鹿鳴》、《四牡》、《皇皇者華》、《魚麗》、《南有嘉魚》、《南山有台》皆用黃鍾清宮。

translations.literal: Minor Odes musical scores: Deer Cry, Four Steeds, Splendid Are the Flowers, Fish Abundant, Southward the Fine Fish, and South Mountain Has Its Terrace all use the Huangzhong clear palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Musical settings for the Minor Odes — "Deer Cry," "Four Steeds," "Splendid Are the Flowers," "Fish Abundant," "Southward the Fine Fish," and "South Mountain Has Its Terrace" — all employ the Huangzhong clear palace mode.

sentences.zh: （俗呼為正宮調。）〉

translations.literal: (commonly called the zhenggong mode.)
translations.idiomatic: (commonly called the zhenggong mode.)

sentences.zh: 二南《國風》詩譜：《關雎》、《葛覃》、《卷耳》、《鵲巢》、《采蘩》、《采蘋》皆用無射清商。

translations.literal: Two Souths Airs of the States musical scores: Ospreys, Kudzu Vine, Ears of Wolf's-tail, Magpie's Nest, Gathering White Artemisia, and Gathering Duckweed all use the Wuye clear shang mode.
translations.idiomatic: Musical settings for the Two Souths in the Airs of the States — "Ospreys," "Kudzu Vine," "Ears of Wolf's-tail," "Magpie's Nest," "Gathering White Artemisia," and "Gathering Duckweed" — all employ the Wuye clear shang mode.

sentences.zh: （俗呼為越調。）〉

translations.literal: (commonly called the yue mode.)
translations.idiomatic: (commonly called the yue mode.)

sentences.zh: 朱熹曰：“《大戴禮》言：《雅》二十六篇，其八可歌，其八廢不可歌，本文頗有闕誤。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said: "The Elder Dai's Record of Rites states: Of the twenty-six pieces of the Ya, eight can be sung and eight were abandoned and cannot be sung; the received text has considerable omissions and errors."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said: "The Elder Dai's Record of Rites states that of the twenty-six Ya pieces, eight can be sung and eight were abandoned as unsingable; the received text contains considerable omissions and errors."

sentences.zh: 漢末杜夔傳舊雅樂四曲：一曰《鹿鳴》，二曰《騶虞》，三曰《伐檀》，又加《文王》詩，皆古聲辭。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Du Kui transmitted four old ya music pieces: first Deer Cry, second Zou Yu, third Felling Sandalwood, with the ode King Wen added as well — all with ancient vocal texts.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Han, Du Kui handed down four pieces of old ya music: "Deer Cry," "Zou Yu," "Felling Sandalwood," and the ode "King Wen" added as well — all with ancient vocal texts.

sentences.zh: 其後，新辭作而舊曲遂廢。

translations.literal: Afterward, new texts were composed and the old melodies were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward new texts were composed and the old melodies fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 唐開元鄉飲酒禮，乃有此十二篇之目，而其聲亦莫得聞。

translations.literal: The Tang Kaiyuan district drinking ceremony listed these twelve pieces, yet their sounds could no longer be heard.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Kaiyuan district drinking ceremony listed these twelve pieces, yet their sounds could no longer be heard.

sentences.zh: 此譜，相傳即開元遺聲也。

translations.literal: These scores are traditionally said to be surviving sounds from the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: These scores are traditionally said to preserve sounds from the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 古聲亡滅已久，不知當時工師何所考而為此。

translations.literal: Ancient sounds have long been lost and extinguished; it is unknown on what basis the craftsmen of that time drew when they made these.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sounds have long since perished; it is unclear what sources the craftsmen of that time drew upon in making these.

sentences.zh: 竊疑古樂有唱、有歎。

translations.literal: I privately suspect that ancient music had lead singing and choral response.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect that ancient music distinguished lead singing from choral response.

sentences.zh: 唱者，發歌句也；

translations.literal: The lead singer utters the lines of the song;
translations.idiomatic: The lead singer utters the lines of the song;

sentences.zh: 和者，繼其聲也。

translations.literal: the chorus continues its sound.
translations.idiomatic: the chorus takes up and continues the sound.

sentences.zh: 詩詞之外，應更有疊字、散聲，以歎發其趣。

translations.literal: Beyond the words of the ode, there should also have been repeated syllables and free vocalizations to draw out its expressive effect.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the words of the ode, there should also have been repeated syllables and free vocalizations to draw out its expressive effect.

sentences.zh: 故漢、晉間舊曲既失其傳，則其詞雖存，而世莫能補。

translations.literal: Therefore, once the old melodies of the Han and Jin periods had lost their transmission, although the texts remained, the world could not restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus once the old melodies of the Han and Jin periods had lost their transmission, although the texts survived, no one in later ages could restore them.

sentences.zh: 如此譜直以一聲協一字，則古詩篇篇可歌。

translations.literal: If a score such as this simply matches one note to one character, then every ancient ode could be sung.
translations.idiomatic: If a score such as this simply matches one note to one character, then every ancient ode could be sung.

sentences.zh: 又其以清聲為調，似亦非古法，然古聲既不可考，姑存此以見聲歌之仿佛，俟知樂者考焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, its use of clear tones as the mode seems also not to be the ancient method; yet since ancient sounds can no longer be verified, these are provisionally preserved to show an approximation of sung poetry, awaiting examination by those who understand music.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, its use of clear tones as the mode seems not to be the ancient method either; yet since ancient sounds can no longer be verified, these scores are provisionally preserved to show an approximation of sung poetry, awaiting examination by those who understand music.

sentences.zh: 琴律賾天地之和者莫如樂，暢樂之趣者莫如琴。

translations.literal: Of what stores the harmony of Heaven and earth, nothing surpasses music; of what gives full expression to music's delight, nothing surpasses the qin.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing stores the harmony of Heaven and earth so fully as music; nothing gives full expression to music's delight so well as the qin.

sentences.zh: 八音以絲為君，絲以琴為君。

translations.literal: Among the eight sounds, silk is sovereign; among silk instruments, the qin is sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Among the eight sounds, silk is paramount; among silk instruments, the qin is paramount.

sentences.zh: 眾器之中，琴德最優。

translations.literal: Among all instruments, the qin's virtue is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Among all instruments, the virtue of the qin is supreme.

sentences.zh: 《白虎通》曰：“琴者，禁止於邪，以正人心也。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of the White Tiger Hall states: "The qin restrains what is depraved and rectifies the human heart."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of the White Tiger Hall states: "The qin restrains what is depraved and rectifies the human heart."

sentences.zh: ”宜眾樂皆為琴之臣妾。

translations.literal: "All music ought to be the qin's servants and handmaids."
translations.idiomatic: All music ought to be the servants and handmaids of the qin.

sentences.zh: 然八音之中，金、石、竹、匏、土、木六者，皆有一定之聲：革為燥濕所薄，絲有弦柱緩急不齊，故二者其聲難定。

translations.literal: Yet among the eight sounds, metal, stone, bamboo, gourd, clay, and wood all have fixed pitches; leather is affected by dryness and moisture, and silk has strings and bridges of uneven tension, so the sounds of these two are hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the eight sounds, metal, stone, bamboo, gourd, clay, and wood all have fixed pitches; leather is affected by dryness and moisture, and silk has strings and bridges of uneven tension, so the pitches of these two are hard to fix.

sentences.zh: 鼓無當於五聲，此不復論。

translations.literal: Drums do not correspond to the five tones; this need not be discussed further.
translations.idiomatic: Drums do not correspond to the five tones; this need not be discussed further.

sentences.zh: 惟絲聲備五聲，而其變無窮。

translations.literal: Only silk sounds possess all five tones, and their variations are inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: Only silk sounds possess all five tones, and their variations are inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 五弦作於虞舜，七弦作於周文、武，此琴製之古者也。

translations.literal: The five-string qin was made by Yu-Shun; the seven-string qin by King Wen and King Wu of Zhou — these are the ancient forms of the instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The five-string qin was made by Yu-Shun; the seven-string qin by King Wen and King Wu of Zhou — these are the ancient forms of the instrument.

sentences.zh: 厥後增損不一。

translations.literal: Afterward additions and reductions were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages added and reduced strings in various ways.

sentences.zh: 至宋始製二弦之琴，以象天地，謂之兩儀琴，每弦各六柱。

translations.literal: It was only in the Song that a two-string qin was first made to represent Heaven and Earth, called the Two Modes qin, each string having six bridges.
translations.idiomatic: It was only in the Song that a two-string qin was first made to represent Heaven and Earth, called the Two Modes qin, with six bridges on each string.

sentences.zh: 又為十二弦以象十二律，其倍應之聲靡不畢備。

translations.literal: A twelve-string qin was also made to represent the twelve pitch standards, and its octave and responding sounds were all completely provided.
translations.idiomatic: A twelve-string qin was also made to represent the twelve pitch standards, with octave and responding tones all fully provided.

sentences.zh: 太宗因大樂雅琴加為九弦，按曲轉入大樂十二律，清濁互相合應。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, taking the great music ceremonial qin, increased it to nine strings; when pieces were played, they shifted into the twelve pitch standards of great music, with clear and muddy tones mutually matching in response.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong increased the great music ceremonial qin to nine strings; when pieces were played, they shifted into the twelve pitch standards of great music, with clear and muddy tones mutually matching in response.

sentences.zh: 大晟樂府嚐罷一、三、七、九。

translations.literal: The Dasheng Music Bureau once abolished the one-, three-, seven-, and nine-string qins.
translations.idiomatic: The Dasheng Music Bureau once abolished the one-, three-, seven-, and nine-string qins.

sentences.zh: 惟存五弦，謂其得五音之正，最優於諸琴也。

translations.literal: Only the five-string qin was retained, on the grounds that it obtained the correctness of the five tones and was superior to all other qins.
translations.idiomatic: Only the five-string qin was retained, on the grounds that it obtained the true five tones and was superior to all other qins.

sentences.zh: 今復俱用。

translations.literal: Now all are used again.
translations.idiomatic: Now all are used again.

sentences.zh: 太常琴製，其長三尺六寸，三百六十分，象周天之度也。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices qin is made three feet six inches long, in three hundred sixty parts, symbolizing the degrees of the circuit of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices qin is three feet six inches long, divided into three hundred sixty parts, symbolizing the degrees of the circuit of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 薑夔《樂議》分琴為三準：自一暉至四暉謂之上準，四寸半，以象黃鍾之半律；

translations.literal: Jiang Kui's Discussion of Music divides the qin into three standards: from the first hui to the fourth hui is called the upper standard, four and a half inches, symbolizing the semitone of Huangzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Kui's Discussion of Music divides the qin into three standards: from the first hui to the fourth hui is the upper standard, four and a half inches, symbolizing the semitone of Huangzhong;

sentences.zh: 自四暉至七暉謂之中準，中準九寸，以象黃鍾之正律；

translations.literal: from the fourth hui to the seventh hui is called the middle standard; the middle standard is nine inches, symbolizing the fundamental pitch of Huangzhong;
translations.idiomatic: from the fourth hui to the seventh hui is the middle standard, nine inches, symbolizing the fundamental pitch of Huangzhong;

sentences.zh: 自七暉至龍齦謂之下準，下準一尺八寸，以象黃鍾之倍律。

translations.literal: from the seventh hui to the dragon gum is called the lower standard; the lower standard is one foot eight inches, symbolizing the octave of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: from the seventh hui to the dragon gum is the lower standard, one foot eight inches, symbolizing the octave of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 三準各具十二律聲，按弦附木而取。

translations.literal: Each of the three standards fully possesses the sounds of the twelve pitch standards, obtained by pressing the string against the wood.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three standards fully possesses the sounds of the twelve pitch standards, obtained by pressing the string against the wood.

sentences.zh: 然須轉弦合本律所用之字，若不轉弦，則誤觸散聲，落別律矣。

translations.literal: Yet the strings must be turned to match the notes used in the fundamental pitch standard; if the strings are not turned, one mistakenly touches open sounds and falls into another pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the strings must be retuned to match the notes used in the fundamental pitch standard; if they are not retuned, one mistakenly touches open sounds and falls into another pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 每一弦各具三十六聲，皆自然也。

translations.literal: Each string in itself possesses thirty-six sounds — all according with nature.
translations.idiomatic: Each string in itself possesses thirty-six sounds — all according with nature.

sentences.zh: 分五、七、九弦琴，各述轉弦合調圖：

translations.literal: For the five-, seven-, and nine-string qins, diagrams of string-turning and mode-matching are set forth separately:
translations.idiomatic: For the five-, seven-, and nine-string qins, diagrams of string retuning and mode matching are set forth separately:

sentences.zh: 《五弦琴圖說》曰：“琴為古樂，所用者皆宮、商、角、徵、羽正音，故以五弦散聲配之。

translations.literal: The Illustrated Explanation of the Five-String Qin states: "The qin is ancient music; what it uses are all the correct tones gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu, and therefore the five open-string sounds are matched to them."
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrated Explanation of the Five-String Qin states: "The qin is ancient music; it uses only the correct tones gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu, and therefore the five open-string sounds are matched to them."

sentences.zh: 其二變之聲，惟用古清商，謂之側弄，不入雅樂。

translations.literal: Its two variant tones use only the ancient clear shang, called side pieces, and do not enter ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: Its two variant tones use only the ancient clear shang, called side pieces, and do not enter ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 《七弦琴圖說》曰：七弦散而扣之，則間一弦於第十暉取應聲。

translations.literal: The Illustrated Explanation of the Seven-String Qin states: When the seven open strings are plucked, one skips a string and takes the responding sound at the tenth hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrated Explanation of the Seven-String Qin states: When the seven open strings are plucked, one skips a string and takes the responding sound at the tenth hui.

sentences.zh: 假如宮調，五弦十暉應七弦散聲，四弦十暉應六弦散聲，二弦十暉應四弦散聲，大弦十暉應三弦散聲，惟三弦獨退一暉，於十一暉應五弦散聲，古今無知之者。

translations.literal: For example, in the gong mode: the fifth string's tenth hui responds to the seventh string's open sound; the fourth string's tenth hui to the sixth string's open sound; the second string's tenth hui to the fourth string's open sound; the great string's tenth hui to the third string's open sound — only the third string alone retreats one hui, responding at the eleventh hui to the fifth string's open sound — a matter unknown in antiquity and the present alike.
translations.idiomatic: For example, in the gong mode: the fifth string's tenth hui responds to the seventh string's open sound; the fourth string's tenth hui to the sixth; the second string's tenth hui to the fourth; the great string's tenth hui to the third — only the third string alone retreats one hui, responding at the eleventh hui to the fifth string's open sound — a matter unknown in antiquity and the present alike.

sentences.zh: 竊謂黃鍾、大呂並用慢角調，故於大弦十一暉應三弦散聲；

translations.literal: I privately hold that Huangzhong and Dalü both use the slow jue mode, and therefore at the great string's eleventh hui one responds to the third string's open sound;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Huangzhong and Dalü both use the slow jue mode, and therefore at the great string's eleventh hui one responds to the third string's open sound;

sentences.zh: 太簇、夾鍾並用清商調，故於二弦方十二暉應四弦散聲；

translations.literal: Taicu and Jiazhong both use the clear shang mode, and therefore at the second string's twelfth hui one responds to the fourth string's open sound;
translations.idiomatic: Taicu and Jiazhong both use the clear shang mode, and therefore at the second string's twelfth hui one responds to the fourth string's open sound;

sentences.zh: 姑洗、仲呂、蕤賓並用宮調，故於三弦十一暉應五弦散聲；

translations.literal: Guxian, Zhonglü, and Ruibin all use the gong mode, and therefore at the third string's eleventh hui one responds to the fifth string's open sound;
translations.idiomatic: Guxian, Zhonglü, and Ruibin all use the gong mode, and therefore at the third string's eleventh hui one responds to the fifth string's open sound;

sentences.zh: 林鍾、夷則並用慢宮調，故於四弦十一暉應六弦散聲；

translations.literal: Linzhong and Yize both use the slow gong mode, and therefore at the fourth string's eleventh hui one responds to the sixth string's open sound;
translations.idiomatic: Linzhong and Yize both use the slow gong mode, and therefore at the fourth string's eleventh hui one responds to the sixth string's open sound;

sentences.zh: 南呂、無射、應鍾並用蕤賓調，故於五弦十一暉應七弦散聲。

translations.literal: Nanlü, Wuye, and Yingzhong all use the ruibin mode, and therefore at the fifth string's eleventh hui one responds to the seventh string's open sound.
translations.idiomatic: Nanlü, Wuye, and Yingzhong all use the ruibin mode, and therefore at the fifth string's eleventh hui one responds to the seventh string's open sound.

sentences.zh: 以律長短配弦大小，各有其序。

translations.literal: Pitch standards of long and short are matched to strings large and small, each in its proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch standards of long and short are matched to strings large and small, each in its proper order.

sentences.zh: 《九弦琴圖說》曰：“弦有七、有九，實即五弦。

translations.literal: The Illustrated Explanation of the Nine-String Qin states: "There are seven strings and there are nine, but in reality these are simply five strings."
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrated Explanation of the Nine-String Qin states: "There are seven strings and there are nine, but in reality these are simply five strings."

sentences.zh: 七弦倍其二，九弦倍其四，所用者五音，亦不以二變為散聲也。

translations.literal: The seven-string qin doubles them by two; the nine-string qin doubles them by four; what is used are the five tones, and the two variants are likewise not taken as open sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The seven-string qin doubles them by two; the nine-string qin doubles them by four; what is used are the five tones, and the two variants are likewise not taken as open sounds.

sentences.zh: 或欲以七弦配五音二變，以餘兩弦為倍，若七弦分配七音，則是今之十四弦也。

translations.literal: Some wish to match the seven strings to the five tones and two variants, taking the remaining two strings as octaves; if seven strings were assigned to seven tones, that would be today's fourteen-string qin.
translations.idiomatic: Some wish to match the seven strings to the five tones and two variants, taking the remaining two strings as octaves; if seven strings were assigned to seven tones, that would be today's fourteen-string qin.

sentences.zh: 《聲律訣》云：‘琴瑟齪四者，律法上下相生也。

translations.literal: The Secrets of Sound and Pitch Standards state: 'The four strings of qin and se — pitch standards generate one another from above to below.'
translations.idiomatic: The Secrets of Sound and Pitch Standards state: "The four strings of qin and se — pitch standards generate one another from above to below."

sentences.zh: ’若加二變，則於律法不諧矣。

translations.literal: 'If the two variants are added, then they will not harmonize with the pitch standards.'
translations.idiomatic: If the two variants are added, they will not harmonize with the pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 或曰：‘如此則琴無二變之聲乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked: 'If so, does the qin then have no sounds of the two variants?'
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "If so, does the qin then have no sounds of the two variants?"

sentences.zh: ’曰：‘附木取之，二變之聲固在也。

translations.literal: 'The answer was: 'Take them by pressing against the wood — the sounds of the two variants are certainly there.''
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: "Take them by pressing against the wood — the sounds of the two variants are certainly there."

sentences.zh: ’合五、七、九弦琴，總述取應聲法，分十二律十二均，每聲取弦暉之應，皆以次列按。

translations.literal: 'For the five-, seven-, and nine-string qins together, the method of taking responding sounds is summarized; divided into twelve pitch standards and twelve keys, for each sound the corresponding string and hui are taken, all listed in order for pressing.'
translations.idiomatic: For the five-, seven-, and nine-string qins together, the method of taking responding sounds is summarized: divided into twelve pitch standards and twelve keys, for each sound the corresponding string and hui are listed in order for pressing.

sentences.zh: 古者大琴則有大瑟，中琴則有中瑟，有雅琴、頌琴，則雅瑟、頌瑟，實為之合。

translations.literal: In antiquity, where there was a great qin there was a great se; where there was a middle qin there was a middle se; where there were ceremonial and hymn qins, there were ceremonial and hymn ses — in reality they were paired together.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, where there was a great qin there was a great se; where there was a middle qin there was a middle se; where there were ceremonial and hymn qins, there were ceremonial and hymn ses — in reality they were paired together.

sentences.zh: 夔乃定瑟之製：桐為背，梓為腹，長九尺九寸，首尾各九寸，隱間八尺一寸，廣尺有八寸，嶽崇寸有八分。

translations.literal: Kui then fixed the se's form: paulownia for the back, catalpa for the belly; length nine feet nine inches, nine inches at head and tail, the concealed span eight feet one inch, width one foot eight inches, bridge height one inch eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: Kui then fixed the se's form: paulownia for the back, catalpa for the belly; nine feet nine inches long, nine inches at head and tail, the sounding span eight feet one inch, one foot eight inches wide, bridges one inch eight fen high.

sentences.zh: 中施九梁，皆象黃鍾之數。

translations.literal: Nine beams were set within, all symbolizing the number of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Nine beams were set within, all symbolizing the number of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁下相連，使其聲衝融；

translations.literal: Below the beams they were joined together so that the sound would blend harmoniously;
translations.idiomatic: Below the beams they were joined together so that the sound would blend harmoniously;

sentences.zh: 首尾之下為兩穴，使其聲條達，是《傳》所謂“大瑟達越”也。

translations.literal: below head and tail were made two holes so that the sound would flow freely — this is what the Commentary calls "the great se's penetrating yue."
translations.idiomatic: below head and tail were made two holes so that the sound would flow freely — this is what the Commentary calls "the great se's penetrating yue."

sentences.zh: 四隅刻雲以緣其武，象其出於雲和。

translations.literal: At the four corners clouds were carved to border its strip (wu), symbolizing that it came from Yunhe.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners clouds were carved along its border strip, symbolizing that the instrument came from Yunhe.

sentences.zh: 漆其壁與首、尾、腹，取椅、桐、梓漆之。

translations.literal: Its walls, head, tail, and belly were lacquered, using varnish from yi, paulownia, and catalpa trees.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls, head, tail, and belly were lacquered with varnish from yi, paulownia, and catalpa.

sentences.zh: 全設二十五弦，弦一柱，崇二寸七分。

translations.literal: Twenty-five strings were set in all, one bridge per string, each bridge two inches seven fen high.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five strings were installed in all, one bridge per string, each bridge two inches and seven fen high.

sentences.zh: 別以五色，五五相次，蒼為上，朱次之，黃次之，素與黔又次之，使肄習者便於擇弦。

translations.literal: They were distinguished by five colors, five and five in succession: blue-green highest, then vermilion, then yellow, then white and black next, so that those practicing could conveniently choose strings.
translations.idiomatic: They were marked in five colors, five and five in succession—blue-green first, then vermilion, then yellow, then white and black—so students could easily choose strings.

sentences.zh: 弦八十一絲而朱之，是謂朱弦。

translations.literal: Each string had eighty-one strands dyed vermilion — this is called the vermilion string.
translations.idiomatic: Each string had eighty-one strands dyed vermilion; this is what is called the vermilion string.

sentences.zh: 其尺則用漢尺。

translations.literal: For measurements the Han foot-rule was used.
translations.idiomatic: Measurements used the Han foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 凡瑟弦具五聲，五聲為均，凡五均，其二變之聲，則柱後抑角、羽而取之，五均凡三十五聲。

translations.literal: In all, se strings possess the five tones; five tones form a key, five keys in all; the two variant tones are taken by pressing behind the bridges to depress jue and yu — five keys totaling thirty-five sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The se strings possess all five tones; five tones form a key, and there are five keys in all. The two variant tones are taken by pressing behind the bridges to depress jue and yu—thirty-five sounds across the five keys.

sentences.zh: 十二律、六十均、四百二十聲，瑟之能事畢矣。

translations.literal: Twelve pitch standards, sixty keys, four hundred twenty sounds — the se's full capacity is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pitch standards, sixty keys, and four hundred twenty sounds—the se's full capacity is complete.

sentences.zh: 夔於琴、瑟之議，其詳如此。

translations.literal: Kui's deliberations on qin and se were this detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's discussion of the qin and se was as detailed as this.

sentences.zh: 朱熹嚐與學者共講琴法，其定律之法：十二律並用太史公九分寸法為準，損益相生，分十二律及五聲，位置各定。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi once lectured on qin method together with students; his method of fixing pitch standards: all twelve pitch standards used Sima Qian's nine-fen-cun method as the standard, diminishing and augmenting to generate one another, dividing into twelve pitch standards and five tones, each position fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once lectured on qin technique together with his students. His method of fixing pitch standards used Sima Qian's nine-fen-cun method for all twelve pitch standards, diminishing and augmenting to generate one another, with twelve pitch standards and five tones each assigned a fixed position.

sentences.zh: 按古人以吹管聲傳於琴上，如吹管起黃鍾，則以琴之黃鍾聲合之；

translations.literal: According to the ancients, the sound of the blown pipe was transmitted onto the qin: if the pipe began on Huangzhong, the qin's Huangzhong sound was matched to it;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients transmitted the sound of the blown pipe onto the qin: if the pipe began on Huangzhong, the qin's Huangzhong tone was matched to it;

sentences.zh: 聲合無差，然後以次遍合諸聲，則五聲皆正。

translations.literal: when the sounds matched without discrepancy, then the remaining sounds were matched in sequence, and the five tones were all correct.
translations.idiomatic: When the sounds matched without discrepancy, the remaining tones were matched in sequence until all five tones were correct.

sentences.zh: 唐人紀琴，先以管色合字定宮弦，乃以宮弦下生徵，徵上生商，上下相生，終於少商。

translations.literal: Tang accounts of the qin first used pipe color to match notes and fix the gong string, then generated zhi below the gong string and shang above it, generating upward and downward until reaching the lesser shang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang accounts of the qin first used pipe color to match notes and fix the gong string, then generated zhi below the gong string and shang above it, generating upward and downward until reaching the lesser shang.

sentences.zh: 下生者隔二弦、上生者隔一弦取之。

translations.literal: For downward generation skip two strings; for upward generation skip one string in taking them.
translations.idiomatic: Downward generation skips two strings; upward generation skips one string.

sentences.zh: 凡絲聲皆當如此。

translations.literal: All silk sounds ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: All silk sounds ought to follow this method.

sentences.zh: 今人苟簡，不復以管定聲，其高下出於臨時，非古法也。

translations.literal: People today are careless and no longer use the pipe to fix the sound; its high and low come from the moment and are not the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: People today are careless and no longer use the pipe to fix pitch; high and low are decided on the spot, which is not the ancient method.

sentences.zh: 調弦之法：散聲隔四而得二聲；

translations.literal: The method of tuning strings: open sounds, skipping four obtain two sounds;
translations.idiomatic: The method of tuning strings: on open strings, skipping four positions yields two sounds;

sentences.zh: 中暉亦如之而得四聲；

translations.literal: the middle hui likewise, obtaining four sounds;
translations.idiomatic: at the middle hui likewise, yielding four sounds;

sentences.zh: 八暉隔三而得六聲；

translations.literal: at the eighth hui, skipping three obtain six sounds;
translations.idiomatic: at the eighth hui, skipping three yields six sounds;

sentences.zh: 九暉按上者隔二而得四聲，按下者隔一而得五聲；

translations.literal: at the ninth hui, pressing above skips two to obtain four sounds, pressing below skips one to obtain five sounds;
translations.idiomatic: at the ninth hui, pressing above skips two to obtain four sounds, pressing below skips one to obtain five sounds;

sentences.zh: 十暉按上者隔一而得五聲，按下者隔二而得四聲。

translations.literal: at the tenth hui, pressing above skips one to obtain five sounds, pressing below skips two to obtain four sounds.
translations.idiomatic: at the tenth hui, pressing above skips one to obtain five sounds, pressing below skips two to obtain four sounds.

sentences.zh: 每疑七弦隔一調之，六弦皆應於第十暉，而第三弦獨於第十一暉調之乃應。

translations.literal: I have long doubted that on the seven-string qin one tunes by skipping one string, and all six strings respond at the tenth hui, yet the third string alone must be tuned at the eleventh hui to respond.
translations.idiomatic: I long doubted why on the seven-string qin one tunes by skipping one string so that six strings respond at the tenth hui, yet the third string alone must be tuned at the eleventh hui to respond.

sentences.zh: 及思而得之，七弦散聲為五聲之正，而大弦十二律之位，又眾弦散聲之所取正也。

translations.literal: On reflection I understood: the seven open strings are the correctness of the five tones, and the great string's positions for the twelve pitch standards are also what all strings' open sounds take as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection I understood: the seven open strings embody the true five tones, and the great string's positions for the twelve pitch standards are also what all strings' open sounds take as their standard.

sentences.zh: 故逐弦之五聲皆自東而西，相為次第。

translations.literal: Therefore the five tones of each string all proceed from east to west in mutual sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the five tones of each string all proceed from east to west in mutual sequence.

sentences.zh: 其六弦會於十暉，則一與三者，角與散角應也；

translations.literal: Where six strings meet at the tenth hui, the first and third are jue responding to open jue;
translations.idiomatic: Where six strings meet at the tenth hui, the first and third are jue responding to open jue;

sentences.zh: 二與四者，徵與散徵應也；

translations.literal: the second and fourth are zhi responding to open zhi;
translations.idiomatic: the second and fourth are zhi responding to open zhi;

sentences.zh: 四與六者，宮與散少宮應也；

translations.literal: the fourth and sixth are gong responding to open lesser gong;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth and sixth are gong responding to open lesser gong;

sentences.zh: 五與七者，商與散少商應也；

translations.literal: the fifth and seventh are shang responding to open lesser shang;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth and seventh are shang responding to open lesser shang;

sentences.zh: 其第三、第五弦會於十一暉，則羽與散羽應也。

translations.literal: the third and fifth strings meet at the eleventh hui, where yu responds to open yu.
translations.idiomatic: the third and fifth strings meet at the eleventh hui, where yu responds to open yu.

sentences.zh: 義各有當，初不相須，故不同會於一暉也。

translations.literal: Each meaning has its proper place and does not depend on the others at first, so they do not all meet at one hui.
translations.idiomatic: Each pairing has its proper rationale and does not depend on the others, so they do not all meet at a single hui.

sentences.zh: 旋宮諸調之法：旋宮古有“隨月用律”之說，今乃謂不必轉軫促弦，但依旋宮之法而抑按之，恐難如此泛論。

translations.literal: The method of rotating keys: in antiquity there was the saying "use pitch standards according to the month"; today it is said that one need not turn pegs or hasten strings but only press according to the rotating-key method — I fear such a broad claim is hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: The method of rotating keys: antiquity had the saying "use pitch standards according to the month"; today some say one need not turn pegs or hasten strings but only press according to the rotating-key method—I fear such a broad claim is hard to sustain.

sentences.zh: 當每宮指定，各以何聲取何弦為唱，各以何弦取何律為均，乃見詳實。

translations.literal: For each palace tone one should specify which sound takes which string as lead, and which string takes which pitch standard as key — only then will it appear detailed and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Each palace tone should specify which sound takes which string as lead and which string takes which pitch standard as key—only then will the account be detailed and solid.

sentences.zh: 又以《禮運正義》推之，則每律各為一宮，每宮各有五調，而其每調用律取聲，亦各有法。

translations.literal: Further, deducing from the Correct Meaning of the Record of Rites, each pitch standard forms one palace, each palace has five modes, and for each mode the use of pitch standards and taking of sounds likewise each has its method.
translations.idiomatic: Further, deducing from the Correct Meaning of the Record of Rites, each pitch standard forms one palace, each palace has five modes, and for each mode the use of pitch standards and taking of sounds each has its method.

sentences.zh: 此為琴之綱領，而說者罕及，乃闕典也。

translations.literal: This is the backbone of the qin, yet expositors rarely reach it — a lacuna in the canon.
translations.idiomatic: This is the backbone of the qin, yet expositors rarely reach it—a lacuna in the canon.

sentences.zh: 當為一圖，以宮統調，以調統聲，令其次第、賓主各有條理。

translations.literal: One should make a diagram with palace governing mode and mode governing sound, so that sequence and principal-subordinate relations each have order.
translations.idiomatic: One should make a diagram with palace governing mode and mode governing sound, so that sequence and principal-subordinate relations each have order.

sentences.zh: 仍先作三圖：一、各具琴之形體、暉弦、尺寸、散聲之位；

translations.literal: First make three diagrams: first, each showing the qin's form, hui, strings, dimensions, and positions of open sounds;
translations.idiomatic: First make three diagrams: first, each showing the qin's form, hui, strings, dimensions, and positions of open sounds;

sentences.zh: 二、附按聲聲律之位；

translations.literal: second, appended with positions of pressed sounds and pitch standards;
translations.idiomatic: second, appended with positions of pressed sounds and pitch standards;

sentences.zh: 三、附泛聲聲律之位，列於宮調圖前，則覽者曉然，可為萬世法矣。

translations.literal: third, appended with positions of harmonic sounds and pitch standards, arrayed before the palace-mode diagram, so viewers will understand clearly and it may serve as law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: third, appended with positions of harmonic sounds and pitch standards, arrayed before the palace-mode diagram, so viewers will understand clearly and it may serve as law for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 觀熹之言，其於琴法本融末粲，至疏達而至縝密，蓋所謂識其大者歟！

translations.literal: Considering Xi's words, his grasp of qin method from root to branch is lucid yet reaches to minute detail — perhaps what is called one who knows the larger pattern!
translations.idiomatic: Considering Xi's words, his grasp of qin method from root to branch is lucid yet reaches minute detail—perhaps what is called knowing the larger pattern!

sentences.zh: 燕樂古者，燕樂自周以來用之。

translations.literal: Yan music: in antiquity, yan music has been used since the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan music: in antiquity, banquet music has been used since the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀增隋九部為十部，以張文收所製歌名燕樂，而被之管弦。

translations.literal: In the Tang Zhenguan reign the Sui nine sections were increased to ten, and Zhang Wenshou's composed songs were named Yan music and fitted to string and wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang Zhenguan reign the Sui nine sections were increased to ten; Zhang Wenshou's composed songs were named Yan music and fitted to strings and winds.

sentences.zh: 厥後至坐部伎琵琶曲，盛流於時，匪直漢氏上林樂府、縵樂不應經法而已。

translations.literal: Later down to the seated-section pipa pieces, they flourished in the age — not merely that the Han Shanglin Music Office and slow music failed to accord with canonical method.
translations.idiomatic: Later, down to the seated-section pipa pieces, they flourished in the age—not merely that the Han Shanglin Music Office and slow music failed to accord with canonical method.

sentences.zh: 宋初置教坊，得江南樂，已汰其坐部不用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song the Music Office was established and obtained Jiangnan music, already discarding the seated section and not using it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song the Music Office was established and obtained Jiangnan music, already discarding the seated section.

sentences.zh: 自後因舊曲創新聲，轉加流麗。

translations.literal: Afterward, on the basis of old melodies new sounds were created, becoming ever more ornate.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, on the basis of old melodies new sounds were created, growing ever more ornate.

sentences.zh: 政和間，詔以大晟雅樂施於燕饗，禦殿按試，補徵、角二調，播之教坊，頒之天下。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era an edict ordered Dasheng ceremonial music applied to banquet entertainment; tested in the imperial hall, the variant zhi and jue modes were supplemented and disseminated to the Music Office and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe era an edict ordered Dasheng ceremonial music applied to banquet entertainment; tested in the imperial hall, the variant zhi and jue modes were supplemented and disseminated to the Music Office and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 然當時樂府奏言：樂之諸宮調多不正，皆俚俗所傳。

translations.literal: Yet at the time the Music Office memorialized that many palace modes of the music were incorrect, all transmitted by vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the time the Music Office reported that many palace modes of the music were incorrect, all transmitted by vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 及命劉昺輯《燕樂新書》，亦惟以八十四調為宗，非復雅音，而曲燕昵狎，至有援“君臣相說之樂”以藉口者。

translations.literal: When Liu Bing was ordered to compile the New Book of Yan Music, he likewise took only the eighty-four modes as the standard, no longer restoring ceremonial tones; banquet music grew intimate and familiar, even citing "music by which ruler and minister delight in one another" as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bing was ordered to compile the New Book of Yan Music, he likewise took only the eighty-four modes as the standard, no longer restoring ceremonial tones; banquet music grew intimate and familiar, even citing "music by which ruler and minister delight in one another" as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 末俗漸靡之弊，愈不容言矣。

translations.literal: The corruption of declining custom grew ever less tolerable to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: The corruption of declining custom grew ever less tolerable to speak of.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，始蠲省教坊樂，凡燕禮，屏坐伎。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era the Music Office music was first abolished; for all banquet rites the seated performers were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaoxing era Music Office music was first abolished; for all banquet rites the seated performers were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乾道繼誌述事，間用雜攢以充教坊之號，取具臨時，而廷紳祝頌，務在嚴恭，亦明以更不用女樂，頒旨子孫守之，以為家法。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao reign, continuing the prior administration, miscellaneous ensembles were occasionally used to fill the name of the Music Office, assembled provisionally; yet at court the nobles' blessings and praises aimed at solemn reverence — it was also made clear that female musicians would no longer be used, an edict issued for descendants to keep as family law.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiandao reign, continuing the prior administration, miscellaneous ensembles were occasionally used to fill the name of the Music Office on a provisional basis; yet at court the nobles' blessings and praises aimed at solemn reverence—it was also made clear that female musicians would no longer be used, with an edict for descendants to keep as family law.

sentences.zh: 於是中興燕樂，比前代猶簡，而有關乎君德者良多。

translations.literal: Thus the restored banquet music of the Zhongxing era was simpler than in prior ages, yet much concerned the ruler's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the restored banquet music of the Zhongxing era was simpler than in prior ages, yet much concerned the ruler's virtue.

sentences.zh: 蔡元定嚐為《燕樂》一書，證俗失以存古義，今采其略附於下：

translations.literal: Cai Yuanding once wrote a book on Yan Music, verifying vulgar errors to preserve ancient meaning; its essentials are excerpted below:
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yuanding once wrote a book on Yan Music, verifying vulgar errors to preserve ancient meaning; its essentials are excerpted below:

sentences.zh: 黃鍾用“合”字，大呂、太簇用“四”字，夾鍾、姑洗用“一”字，夷則、南呂用“工”字，無射、應鍾用“凡”字，各以上、下分為清濁。

translations.literal: Huangzhong uses the note "he," Dalü and Taicu use "si," Jiazhong and Guxian use "yi," Yize and Nanlü use "gong," Wuye and Yingzhong use "fan," each divided into clear and muddy by upper and lower.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong uses the note "he," Dalü and Taicu use "si," Jiazhong and Guxian use "yi," Yize and Nanlü use "gong," Wuye and Yingzhong use "fan," each divided into clear and muddy by upper and lower.

sentences.zh: 其中呂、蕤賓、林鍾不可以上、下分，中呂用“上”字，蕤賓用“勾”字，林鍾用“尺”字。

translations.literal: Among them Zhonglü, Ruibin, and Linzhong cannot be divided by upper and lower: Zhonglü uses "shang," Ruibin uses "gou," Linzhong uses "chi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü, Ruibin, and Linzhong cannot be divided by upper and lower: Zhonglü uses "shang," Ruibin uses "gou," Linzhong uses "chi."

sentences.zh: 其黃鍾清用“ 六”字，大呂、太簇、夾鍾清各用“五”字，而以下、上、緊別之。

translations.literal: Clear Huangzhong uses "liu," clear Dalü, Taicu, and Jiazhong each use "wu," distinguished by lower, upper, and tight.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Huangzhong uses "liu," clear Dalü, Taicu, and Jiazhong each use "wu," distinguished by lower, upper, and tight.

sentences.zh: 緊“五”者，夾鍾清聲，俗樂以為宮。

translations.literal: "Tight wu" is the clear sound of Jiazhong; vulgar music takes it as gong.
translations.idiomatic: "Tight wu" is the clear sound of Jiazhong; vulgar music takes it as gong.

sentences.zh: 此其取律寸、律數、用字紀聲之略也。

translations.literal: This is the summary of taking pitch-standard inches, pitch-standard numbers, and using characters to record sounds.
translations.idiomatic: This is the summary of taking pitch-standard inches, pitch-standard numbers, and using characters to record sounds.

sentences.zh: 一宮、二商、三角、四變為宮，五徵、六羽、七閏為角。

translations.literal: First gong, second shang, third jue, fourth variant as gong, fifth zhi, sixth yu, seventh intercalary as jue.
translations.idiomatic: First gong, second shang, third jue, fourth variant as gong, fifth zhi, sixth yu, seventh intercalary as jue.

sentences.zh: 五聲之號與雅樂同，惟變徵以於十二律中陰陽易位，故謂之變。

translations.literal: The names of the five tones are the same as in ceremonial music; only variant zhi shifts yin and yang positions among the twelve pitch standards, hence called "variant."
translations.idiomatic: The names of the five tones are the same as in ceremonial music; only variant zhi shifts yin and yang positions among the twelve pitch standards, hence called "variant."

sentences.zh: 變宮以七聲所不及，取閏餘之義，故謂之閏。

translations.literal: Variant gong takes what the seven tones do not reach, borrowing the meaning of the intercalary remainder, hence called "intercalary."
translations.idiomatic: Variant gong takes what the seven tones do not reach, borrowing the meaning of the intercalary remainder, hence called "intercalary."

sentences.zh: 四變居宮聲之對，故為宮。

translations.literal: The fourth variant stands opposite gong, therefore it counts as gong.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth variant stands opposite gong, therefore it counts as gong.

sentences.zh: 俗樂以閏為正聲，以閏加變，故閏為角而實非正角。

translations.literal: Vulgar music takes intercalary as a correct tone; adding variant to intercalary, intercalary becomes jue though in reality it is not true jue.
translations.idiomatic: Vulgar music takes intercalary as a correct tone; adding variant to intercalary, intercalary becomes jue though in reality it is not true jue.

sentences.zh: 此其七聲高下之略也。

translations.literal: This is the summary of the seven tones' high and low.
translations.idiomatic: This is the summary of the seven tones' high and low.

sentences.zh: 聲由陽來，陽生於子、終於午。

translations.literal: Sound comes from yang; yang is born at zi and ends at wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sound comes from yang; yang is born at zi and ends at wu.

sentences.zh: 燕樂以夾鍾收四聲：曰宮、曰商、曰羽、曰閏。

translations.literal: Yan music takes Jiazhong to gather four sounds: called gong, shang, yu, and intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: Yan music takes Jiazhong to gather four sounds: called gong, shang, yu, and intercalary.

sentences.zh: 閏為角，其正角聲、變聲、徵聲皆不收，而獨用夾鍾為律本。

translations.literal: Intercalary serves as jue; true jue, variant sound, and zhi sound are all not gathered, and Jiazhong alone is taken as the pitch-standard root.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary serves as jue; true jue, variant sound, and zhi sound are all not gathered, and Jiazhong alone is taken as the pitch-standard root.

sentences.zh: 此其夾鍾收四聲之略也。

translations.literal: This is the summary of Jiazhong gathering four sounds.
translations.idiomatic: This is the summary of Jiazhong gathering four sounds.

sentences.zh: 宮聲七調：曰正宮、曰高宮、曰中呂宮、曰道宮、曰南呂宮、曰仙呂宮、曰黃鍾宮，皆生於黃鍾。

translations.literal: Gong-tone seven modes: Zhenggong, Gaogong, Zhonglü palace, Daodiao palace, Nanlü palace, Xianlü palace, Huangzhong palace — all generated from Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong-tone seven modes: Zhenggong, Gaogong, Zhonglü palace, Daodiao palace, Nanlü palace, Xianlü palace, Huangzhong palace—all generated from Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 商聲七調：曰大食調、曰高大食調、曰雙調、曰小食調、曰歇指調、曰商調、曰越調，皆生於太簇。

translations.literal: Shang-tone seven modes: Dashi mode, Gaodashi mode, Shuang mode, Xiaoshi mode, Xiezhi mode, Shang mode, Yue mode — all generated from Taicu.
translations.idiomatic: Shang-tone seven modes: Dashi mode, Gaodashi mode, Shuang mode, Xiaoshi mode, Xiezhi mode, Shang mode, Yue mode—all generated from Taicu.

sentences.zh: 羽聲七調：曰般涉調、曰高般涉調、曰中呂調、曰正平調、曰南呂調、曰仙呂調、曰黃鍾調，皆生於南呂。

translations.literal: Yu-tone seven modes: Banshe mode, Gaobanshe mode, Zhonglü mode, Zhengping mode, Nanlü mode, Xianlü mode, Huangzhong mode — all generated from Nanlü.
translations.idiomatic: Yu-tone seven modes: Banshe mode, Gaobanshe mode, Zhonglü mode, Zhengping mode, Nanlü mode, Xianlü mode, Huangzhong mode—all generated from Nanlü.

sentences.zh: 角聲七調：曰大食角、曰高大食角、曰雙角、曰小食角、曰歇指角、曰商角、曰越角、皆生於應鍾。

translations.literal: Jue-tone seven modes: Dashi jue, Gaodashi jue, Shuang jue, Xiaoshi jue, Xiezhi jue, Shang jue, Yue jue — all generated from Yingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jue-tone seven modes: Dashi jue, Gaodashi jue, Shuang jue, Xiaoshi jue, Xiezhi jue, Shang jue, Yue jue—all generated from Yingzhong.

sentences.zh: 此其四聲二十八調之略也。

translations.literal: This is the summary of the four sounds' twenty-eight modes.
translations.idiomatic: This is the summary of the four sounds' twenty-eight modes.

sentences.zh: 竊考元定言燕樂大要，其律本出夾鍾，以十二律兼四清為十六聲，而夾鍾為最清，此所謂靡靡之聲也。

translations.literal: On examination, Yuanding's account of yan music in essence takes Jiazhong as the pitch-standard root, using twelve pitch standards together with four clear tones as sixteen sounds, and Jiazhong as the clearest — this is what is called decadent sound.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, Yuanding's account of yan music in essence takes Jiazhong as the pitch-standard root, using twelve pitch standards together with four clear tones as sixteen sounds, with Jiazhong the clearest—this is what is called decadent sound.

sentences.zh: 觀其律本，則其樂可知。

translations.literal: Observing its pitch-standard root, its music may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Observing its pitch-standard root, its music may be known.

sentences.zh: 變宮、變徵既非正聲，而以變徵為宮，以變宮為角，反紊亂正聲。

translations.literal: Variant gong and variant zhi are not correct tones; yet taking variant zhi as gong and variant gong as jue reverses and disorders the correct tones.
translations.idiomatic: Variant gong and variant zhi are not correct tones; yet taking variant zhi as gong and variant gong as jue reverses and disorders the correct tones.

sentences.zh: 若此夾鍾宮謂之中呂宮、林鍾宮謂之南呂宮者，燕樂聲高，實以夾鍾為黃鍾也。

translations.literal: Where this Jiazhong palace is called Zhonglü palace and Linzhong palace is called Nanlü palace, yan music's pitch is high — in reality Jiazhong serves as Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Where Jiazhong palace is called Zhonglü palace and Linzhong palace is called Nanlü palace, yan music's pitch is high—in reality Jiazhong serves as Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 所收二十八調，本萬寶常所謂非治世之音，俗又於七角調各加一聲，流蕩忘反，而祖調亦不復存矣。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight modes gathered were originally what Wan Baochang called sounds not of an age of good government; vulgar custom again added one sound to each of the seven jue modes, flowing and forgetting to return, and the ancestral modes likewise no longer survived.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight modes gathered were originally what Wan Baochang called sounds not of an age of good government; vulgar custom again added one sound to each of the seven jue modes, flowing and forgetting to return, and the ancestral modes no longer survived.

sentences.zh: 聲之感人，如風偃草，宜風俗之日衰也！

translations.literal: Sound's moving of people is like wind laying grass low — fitting that custom daily declines!
translations.idiomatic: Sound's moving of people is like wind laying grass low—fitting that custom daily declines!

sentences.zh: 夫奸聲亂色，不留聰明；

translations.literal: Depraved sound and disorderly color do not lodge in clear hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Depraved sound and disorderly color do not lodge in clear hearing;

sentences.zh: 淫樂慝禮，不接心術。

translations.literal: licentious music and perverse rite do not connect with the heart's art.
translations.idiomatic: licentious music and perverse rite do not connect with the heart's art.

sentences.zh: 使心知百體，皆由順正以行其義，此正古君子所以為治天下之本也。

translations.literal: Let the mind know that the hundred parts all proceed by rectifying correctness to enact their principles — this is why the ancient gentleman made governing the world his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Let the mind know that the hundred parts all proceed by rectifying correctness to enact their principles—this is why the ancient gentleman made governing the world his foundation.

sentences.zh: 紹興、乾道教坊迄弛不復置雲。

translations.literal: From Shaoxing and Qiandao onward the Music Office was abolished and never re-established.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaoxing and Qiandao onward the Music Office was abolished and never re-established.

sentences.zh: 教坊自唐武德以來，置署在禁門內。

translations.literal: The Music Office, since the Tang Wude era, was established within the forbidden gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office, since the Tang Wude era, was established within the forbidden gate.

sentences.zh: 開元後，其人浸多，凡祭祀、大朝會則用太常雅樂，歲時宴享則用教坊諸部樂。

translations.literal: After the Kaiyuan reign its personnel gradually increased; for sacrifices and great court assemblies the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ceremonial music was used, and for seasonal banquets the Music Office's various section music.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaiyuan reign its personnel gradually increased; for sacrifices and great court assemblies the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ceremonial music was used, and for seasonal banquets the Music Office's various section music.

sentences.zh: 前代有宴樂、清樂、散樂，本隸太常，後稍歸教坊，有立、坐二部。

translations.literal: Prior ages had banquet music, pure music, and scattered music, originally subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; later they gradually passed to the Music Office, with standing and seated two sections.
translations.idiomatic: Prior ages had banquet music, pure music, and scattered music, originally subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; later they gradually passed to the Music Office, with standing and seated two sections.

sentences.zh: 宋初循舊制，置教坊，凡四部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song the old system was followed and the Music Office established — four sections in all.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song the old system was followed and the Music Office established—four sections in all.

sentences.zh: 其後平荊南，得樂工三十二人；

translations.literal: Later, pacifying Jingnan, thirty-two musicians were obtained;
translations.idiomatic: Later, pacifying Jingnan, thirty-two musicians were obtained;

sentences.zh: 平西川，得一百三十九人；

translations.literal: pacifying Xichuan, one hundred thirty-nine;
translations.idiomatic: pacifying Xichuan, one hundred thirty-nine;

sentences.zh: 平江南，得十六人；

translations.literal: pacifying Jiangnan, sixteen;
translations.idiomatic: pacifying Jiangnan, sixteen;

sentences.zh: 平太原，得十九人；

translations.literal: pacifying Taiyuan, nineteen;
translations.idiomatic: pacifying Taiyuan, nineteen;

sentences.zh: 餘藩臣所貢者八十三人；

translations.literal: further musicians presented by remaining feudatory ministers, eighty-three;
translations.idiomatic: further musicians presented by remaining feudatory ministers, eighty-three;

sentences.zh: 又太宗藩邸有七十一人。

translations.literal: and from Taizong's princely residence, seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: and from Taizong's princely residence, seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 由是，四方執藝之精者皆在籍中。

translations.literal: Thus the finest performers from the four quarters were all on the register.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the finest performers from the four quarters were all on the register.

sentences.zh: 每春秋聖節三大宴：其第一、皇帝升坐，宰相進酒，庭中吹觱栗，以眾樂和之；

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn, on the three great festival days of the sage's birthday: first, the emperor ascends and sits, the chief minister presents wine, and in the courtyard the bili pipe is blown with all music harmonizing;
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn, on the three great festival days of the sage's birthday: first, the emperor ascends and sits, the chief minister presents wine, and in the courtyard the bili pipe is blown with all music harmonizing;

sentences.zh: 賜群臣酒，皆就坐，宰相飲，作《傾杯樂》；

translations.literal: wine is granted to the ministers, all taking their seats; when the chief minister drinks, "Tipping Cup Music" is performed;
translations.idiomatic: wine is granted to the ministers, all taking their seats; when the chief minister drinks, "Tipping Cup Music" is performed;

sentences.zh: 百官飲，作《三台》。

translations.literal: when the hundred officials drink, "Three Platforms" is performed.
translations.idiomatic: when the hundred officials drink, "Three Platforms" is performed.

sentences.zh: 第二、皇帝再舉酒，群臣立於席後，樂以歌起。

translations.literal: Second: the emperor raises wine again; the ministers stand behind their mats and music begins with song.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the emperor raises wine again; the ministers stand behind their mats and music begins with song.

sentences.zh: 第三、皇帝舉酒，如第二之製，以次進食。

translations.literal: Third: the emperor raises wine as in the second item, and food is brought in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the emperor raises wine as in the second item, and food is brought in succession.

sentences.zh: 第四、百戲皆作。

translations.literal: Fourth: the hundred entertainments are all performed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: the hundred entertainments are all performed.

sentences.zh: 第五、皇帝舉酒，如第二之製。

translations.literal: Fifth: the emperor raises wine as in the second item.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the emperor raises wine as in the second item.

sentences.zh: 第六、樂工致辭，繼以詩一章，謂之“口號”，皆述德美及中外蹈詠之情。

translations.literal: Sixth: the music workers deliver a formal address, followed by one stanza of poetry, called a "kouhao" (oral proclamation); all describe virtue and beauty and the feelings of court and commoners treading and singing in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: the musicians deliver a formal address, then a single poem called a kouhao—an oral proclamation—all praising imperial virtue and the joy with which those at court and abroad alike tread the measure and sing in celebration.

sentences.zh: 初致辭，群臣皆起，聽辭畢，再拜。

translations.literal: When the address is first delivered, all ministers rise; when the address is finished, they listen to its completion and bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the address all ministers rise; when it is finished they bow twice.

sentences.zh: 第七、合奏大曲。

translations.literal: Seventh: combined performance of a grand suite.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: a grand suite is performed in ensemble.

sentences.zh: 第八、皇帝舉酒，殿上獨彈琵琶。

translations.literal: Eighth: the emperor raises his cup; on the dais the pipa alone is played.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: the emperor raises his cup while a solo pipa is played upon the dais.

sentences.zh: 第九、小兒隊舞，亦致辭以述德美。

translations.literal: Ninth: the boys' troupe dance; they also deliver an address to set forth virtue and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: the boys' dance troupe performs, likewise delivering an address in praise of virtue.

sentences.zh: 第十、雜劇。

translations.literal: Tenth: miscellaneous plays.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: variety skits.

sentences.zh: 罷，皇帝起更衣。

translations.literal: When [these] end, the emperor rises to change his robes.
translations.idiomatic: When they are finished, the emperor rises to change his robes.

sentences.zh: 第十一、皇帝再坐，舉酒，殿上獨吹笙。

translations.literal: Eleventh: the emperor sits again, raises his cup; on the dais the sheng alone is blown.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh: the emperor sits again and raises his cup while a solo sheng is played upon the dais.

sentences.zh: 第十二、蹴踘。

translations.literal: Twelfth: cuju.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth: cuju kickball.

sentences.zh: 第十三、皇帝舉酒，殿上獨彈箏。

translations.literal: Thirteenth: the emperor raises his cup; on the dais the zheng alone is plucked.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth: the emperor raises his cup while a solo zheng is played upon the dais.

sentences.zh: 第十四、女弟子隊舞，亦致辭如小兒隊。

translations.literal: Fourteenth: the female disciples' troupe dance; they also deliver an address as the boys' troupe does.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth: the female disciples' dance troupe performs, delivering an address in the same manner as the boys' troupe.

sentences.zh: 第十五、雜劇。

translations.literal: Fifteenth: miscellaneous plays.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth: variety skits.

sentences.zh: 第十六、皇帝舉酒，如第二之製。

translations.literal: Sixteenth: the emperor raises his cup, as in the second item's procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth: the emperor raises his cup according to the procedure of the second item.

sentences.zh: 第十七、奏鼓吹曲，或用法曲，或用《龜茲》。

translations.literal: Seventeenth: wind-and-drum suites are performed, either court suite music (fayue) or the suite "Kuche."
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth: wind-and-drum suites are performed, either fayue court suites or the "Kuche" suite.

sentences.zh: 第十八、皇帝舉酒，如第二之製，食罷。

translations.literal: Eighteenth: the emperor raises his cup, as in the second item's procedure; the meal is finished.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth: the emperor raises his cup according to the procedure of the second item, and the meal concludes.

sentences.zh: 第十九、用角，宴畢。

translations.literal: Nineteenth: juedi [grappling entertainment] is performed; the feast is concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth: juedi performances are presented, and the great feast ends.

sentences.zh: 其禦樓賜酺同大宴。

translations.literal: Imperial-bestowed libations from the tower follow the same procedure as the great feast.
translations.idiomatic: Libations bestowed from the imperial tower follow the same program as the great feast.

sentences.zh: 崇德殿宴契丹使，惟無後場雜劇及女弟子舞隊。

translations.literal: At banquets for Khitan envoys in the Chongde Hall, only the rear-court miscellaneous plays and the female disciples' dance troupe were omitted.
translations.idiomatic: When entertaining Khitan envoys in the Chongde Hall, only the rear-court variety skits and the female disciples' dance troupe were omitted.

sentences.zh: 每上元觀燈，樓前設露台，台上奏教坊樂、舞小兒隊。

translations.literal: On each Lantern Festival when lamps are viewed, a terrace stage is set before the tower; on the stage the Music Office performs and the boys' troupe dances.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the Lantern Festival, when lamps are displayed, a terrace stage is erected before the tower; upon it the Music Office plays and the boys' troupe dances.

sentences.zh: 台南設燈山，燈山前陳百戲，山棚上用散樂、女弟子舞。

translations.literal: South of the stage a lamp mountain is set up; before the lamp mountain a hundred entertainments are arrayed; on the mountain scaffold scattered music and the female disciples' dance are performed.
translations.idiomatic: South of the stage stands a lamp mountain; before it a hundred acts are staged, while on the mountain scaffold scattered music and the female disciples' dance are performed.

sentences.zh: 餘曲宴會、賞花、習射、觀稼，凡遊幸但奏樂行酒，惟慶節上壽及將相入辭賜酒，則止奏樂。

translations.literal: At remaining informal banquets, flower-viewing, archery practice, and inspecting the crops—as well as all imperial excursions—only music is played while wine is served; only at celebrations of felicitous days, birthday felicitations, and when chief ministers take leave and are granted wine is music alone performed.
translations.idiomatic: At other informal banquets, flower-viewing, archery, and crop inspections, and on all imperial excursions, music accompanies the serving of wine alone; only on felicitous holidays, birthday celebrations, and when chief ministers take leave and receive granted wine is music performed without the full feast program.

sentences.zh: （都知、色長二人攝太官令，升殿對立，逡巡周，大宴則酒、唱遍，曲宴宰相雖各舉酒，通用慢曲而舞《三台》。）〉

translations.literal: (Two directors and lead performers act as Grand Stewards pro tempore, ascend the hall and stand facing each other, and pace the circuit; at the great feast there is wine and singing through to completion; at informal banquets for chief ministers, though each raises wine separately, they uniformly use slow suites and dance "Three Platforms.")
translations.idiomatic: (Two directors and lead performers of the Music Office act as Grand Stewards pro tempore, ascend the hall and stand opposite one another, and pace the circuit. At the great feast wine is served and the suite is sung through to completion; at informal banquets for chief ministers, though each raises wine in turn, they uniformly use slow suites and dance "Three Platforms.")

sentences.zh: 所奏凡十八調、四十大曲：一曰正宮調，其曲三，曰《梁州》、《瀛府》、《齊天樂》；

translations.literal: What was performed comprised eighteen modes and forty grand suites: first, Zhenggong mode, with three suites, namely "Liangzhou," "Yingfu," and "Qitian Le";
translations.idiomatic: In all, eighteen modes and forty grand suites were performed. First, Zhenggong mode, with three suites: "Liangzhou," "Yingfu," and "Qitian Le";

sentences.zh: 二曰中呂宮，其曲二，曰《萬年歡》、《劍器》；

translations.literal: second, Zhonglü palace mode, with two suites, namely "Wannian Huan" and "Jianqi";
translations.idiomatic: second, Zhonglü palace mode, with two suites: "Wannian Huan" and "Jianqi";

sentences.zh: 三曰道調宮，其曲三，曰《梁州》、《薄媚》、《大聖樂》；

translations.literal: third, Daodiao palace mode, with three suites, namely "Liangzhou," "Bomei," and "Dasheng Le";
translations.idiomatic: third, Daodiao palace mode, with three suites: "Liangzhou," "Bomei," and "Dasheng Le";

sentences.zh: 四曰南呂宮，其曲二，曰《瀛府》、《薄媚》；

translations.literal: fourth, Nanlü palace mode, with two suites, namely "Yingfu" and "Bomei";
translations.idiomatic: fourth, Nanlü palace mode, with two suites: "Yingfu" and "Bomei";

sentences.zh: 五曰仙呂宮，其曲三，曰《梁州》、《保金枝》、《延壽樂》；

translations.literal: fifth, Xianlü palace mode, with three suites, namely "Liangzhou," "Baojin Zhi," and "Yanshou Le";
translations.idiomatic: fifth, Xianlü palace mode, with three suites: "Liangzhou," "Baojin Zhi," and "Yanshou Le";

sentences.zh: 六曰黃鍾宮，其曲三，曰《梁州》、《中和樂》、《劍器》；

translations.literal: sixth, Huangzhong palace mode, with three suites, namely "Liangzhou," "Zhonghe Le," and "Jianqi";
translations.idiomatic: sixth, Huangzhong palace mode, with three suites: "Liangzhou," "Zhonghe Le," and "Jianqi";

sentences.zh: 七曰越調，其曲二，曰《伊州》、《石州》；

translations.literal: seventh, Yue mode, with two suites, namely "Yizhou" and "Shizhou";
translations.idiomatic: seventh, Yue mode, with two suites: "Yizhou" and "Shizhou";

sentences.zh: 八曰大石調，其曲二，曰《清平樂》、《大明樂》；

translations.literal: eighth, Dashi mode, with two suites, namely "Qingping Le" and "Daming Le";
translations.idiomatic: eighth, Dashi mode, with two suites: "Qingping Le" and "Daming Le";

sentences.zh: 九曰雙調，其曲三，曰《降聖樂》、《新水調》、《采蓮》；

translations.literal: ninth, Shuang mode, with three suites, namely "Jiangsheng Le," "Xin Shuidiao," and "Cailian";
translations.idiomatic: ninth, Shuang mode, with three suites: "Jiangsheng Le," "Xin Shuidiao," and "Cailian";

sentences.zh: 十曰小石調，其曲二，曰《胡渭州》、《嘉慶樂》；

translations.literal: tenth, Xiaoshi mode, with two suites, namely "Hu Weizhou" and "Jiaqing Le";
translations.idiomatic: tenth, Xiaoshi mode, with two suites: "Hu Weizhou" and "Jiaqing Le";

sentences.zh: 十一曰歇指調，其曲三，曰《伊州》、《君臣相遇樂》、《慶雲樂》；

translations.literal: eleventh, Xiezhi mode, with three suites, namely "Yizhou," "Junchen Xiangyu Le," and "Qingyun Le";
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, Xiezhi mode, with three suites: "Yizhou," "Junchen Xiangyu Le," and "Qingyun Le";

sentences.zh: 十二曰林鍾商，其曲三，曰《賀皇恩》、《泛清波》、《胡渭州》；

translations.literal: twelfth, Linzhong shang mode, with three suites, namely "He Huang'en," "Fan Qingbo," and "Hu Weizhou";
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, Linzhong shang mode, with three suites: "He Huang'en," "Fan Qingbo," and "Hu Weizhou";

sentences.zh: 十三曰中呂調，其曲二，曰《綠腰》、《道人歡》；

translations.literal: thirteenth, Zhonglü mode, with two suites, namely "Lüyao" and "Daoren Huan";
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth, Zhonglü mode, with two suites: "Lüyao" and "Daoren Huan";

sentences.zh: 十四曰南呂調，其曲二，曰《綠腰》《罷金鉦》；

translations.literal: fourteenth, Nanlü mode, with two suites, namely "Lüyao" and "Ba Jin Zheng";
translations.idiomatic: fourteenth, Nanlü mode, with two suites: "Lüyao" and "Ba Jin Zheng";

sentences.zh: 十五曰仙呂調，其曲二，曰《綠腰》、《采雲歸》；

translations.literal: fifteenth, Xianlü mode, with two suites, namely "Lüyao" and "Caiyun Gui";
translations.idiomatic: fifteenth, Xianlü mode, with two suites: "Lüyao" and "Caiyun Gui";

sentences.zh: 十六曰黃鍾羽，其曲一，曰《千春樂》；

translations.literal: sixteenth, Huangzhong yu mode, with one suite, namely "Qianchun Le";
translations.idiomatic: sixteenth, Huangzhong yu mode, with one suite: "Qianchun Le";

sentences.zh: 十七曰般涉調，其曲二，曰《長壽仙》、《滿宮春》；

translations.literal: seventeenth, Banshe mode, with two suites, namely "Changshou Xian" and "Man Gongchun";
translations.idiomatic: seventeenth, Banshe mode, with two suites: "Changshou Xian" and "Man Gongchun";

sentences.zh: 十八曰正平調，無大曲，小曲無定數。

translations.literal: eighteenth, Zhengping mode, with no grand suite; small suites are without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: eighteenth, Zhengping mode, which had no grand suite; the number of small suites was not fixed.

sentences.zh: 不用者有十調：一曰高宮，二曰高大石，三曰高般涉，四曰越角，五曰大石角，六曰高大石角，七曰雙角，八曰小石角，九曰歇指角，十曰林鍾角。

translations.literal: Ten modes not used: first, Gaogong; second, Gaodashi; third, Gaobanshe; fourth, Yuejiao; fifth, Dashi jiao; sixth, Gaodashi jiao; seventh, Shuangjiao; eighth, Xiaoshi jiao; ninth, Xiezhi jiao; tenth, Linzhong jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ten modes were not used: Gaogong, Gaodashi, Gaobanshe, Yuejiao, Dashi jiao, Gaodashi jiao, Shuangjiao, Xiaoshi jiao, Xiezhi jiao, and Linzhong jiao.

sentences.zh: 樂用琵琶、箜篌、五弦琴、箏、笙、觱栗、笛、方響、羯鼓、杖鼓、拍板。

translations.literal: The music employed the pipa, konghou, five-string zither, zheng, sheng, bili pipe, flute, fangxiang, jie drum, staff drum, and clappers.
translations.idiomatic: The ensemble used pipa, konghou, five-string zither, zheng, sheng, bili pipe, flute, fangxiang metallophone, jie drum, staff drum, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 法曲部，其曲二，一曰道調宮《望瀛》，二曰小石調《獻仙音》。

translations.literal: Fayue section: two suites—first, Daodiao palace mode "Wangying"; second, Xiaoshi mode "Xianxian Yin."
translations.idiomatic: The fayue section had two suites: Daodiao palace mode, "Wangying"; and Xiaoshi mode, "Xianxian Yin."

sentences.zh: 樂用琵琶、箜篌、五弦、箏、笙、觱栗、方響、拍板。

translations.literal: Music employed the pipa, konghou, five-string [zither], zheng, sheng, bili pipe, fangxiang, and clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments were pipa, konghou, five-string zither, zheng, sheng, bili pipe, fangxiang, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 龜茲部，其曲二，皆雙調，一曰《宇宙清》，二曰《感皇恩》。

translations.literal: Kuche section: two suites, both in Shuang mode—first, "Yuzhou Qing"; second, "Gan Huang'en."
translations.idiomatic: The Kuche section had two suites, both in Shuang mode: "Yuzhou Qing" and "Gan Huang'en."

sentences.zh: 樂用觱栗、笛、羯鼓、腰鼓、揩鼓、雞樓鼓、鞀鼓、拍板。

translations.literal: Music employed the bili pipe, flute, jie drum, waist drum, kai drum, chicken-tower drum, taogu, and clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Its instruments were bili pipe, flute, jie drum, waist drum, kai drum, chicken-tower drum, taogu, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 鼓笛部，樂用三色笛、杖鼓、拍板。

translations.literal: Drum-and-flute section: music employed three-color flutes, staff drum, and clappers.
