translations.idiomatic: The drum-and-flute section used three-color flutes, staff drum, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 隊舞之製，其名各十。

translations.literal: The regulations for troupe dance: their names are ten each.
translations.idiomatic: The system of troupe dance comprised ten names for each category.

sentences.zh: 小兒隊凡七十二人：一曰柘枝隊，衣五色繡羅寬袍，戴胡帽，係銀帶；

translations.literal: The boys' troupe numbered seventy-two in all: first, the Zhezhi troupe, wearing five-colored embroidered silk wide robes, donning foreign caps, girded with silver belts;
translations.idiomatic: The boys' troupe comprised seventy-two dancers in all. First, the Zhezhi troupe, in five-colored embroidered silk wide robes, foreign caps, and silver belts;

sentences.zh: 二曰劍器隊，衣五色繡羅襦，裹交腳襆頭，紅羅繡抹額，帶器仗；

translations.literal: second, the Jianqi troupe, wearing five-colored embroidered silk jackets, wrapped cross-legged turbans, red silk embroidered forehead bands, and carrying weapons;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Jianqi troupe, in five-colored embroidered silk jackets, cross-legged turbans, red silk embroidered forehead bands, and bearing weapons;

sentences.zh: 三曰婆羅門隊，紫羅僧衣，緋掛子，執錫鐶拄杖；

translations.literal: third, the Brahmana troupe, in purple silk monastic robes and scarlet hanging panels, holding tin-ringed staffs;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Brahmana troupe, in purple silk monastic robes and scarlet hanging panels, bearing tin-ringed staffs;

sentences.zh: 四曰醉胡騰隊，衣紅錦襦，係銀舌鞢，戴氈帽；

translations.literal: fourth, the Drunken Huteng troupe, wearing red brocade jackets, girded with silver-trimmed boots, and donning felt caps;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Drunken Huteng troupe, in red brocade jackets, silver-trimmed boots, and felt caps;

sentences.zh: 五曰諢臣萬歲樂隊，衣紫緋綠羅寬衫，諢裹簇花襆頭；

translations.literal: fifth, the Jester-Minister Wansui Le troupe, wearing purple, scarlet, and green silk wide shirts, jest-wrapped clustered-flower turbans;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Jester-Minister Wansui Le troupe, in purple, scarlet, and green silk wide shirts and jest-wrapped clustered-flower turbans;

sentences.zh: 六曰兒童感聖樂隊，衣青羅生色衫，係勒帛，總兩角；

translations.literal: sixth, the Children's Gansheng Le troupe, wearing blue silk raw-color shirts, girded with restraining silks, hair bound in two horns;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the Children's Gansheng Le troupe, in blue silk shirts of raw dye, with restraining silks and hair bound in two topknots;

sentences.zh: 七曰玉兔渾脫隊，四色繡羅襦，係銀帶，冠玉兔冠；

translations.literal: seventh, the Jade Rabbit Huntuo troupe, in four-colored embroidered silk jackets, girded with silver belts, crowned with jade-rabbit crowns;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, the Jade Rabbit Huntuo troupe, in four-colored embroidered silk jackets, silver belts, and jade-rabbit crowns;

sentences.zh: 八曰異域朝天隊，衣錦襖，係銀束帶，冠夷冠，執寶盤；

translations.literal: eighth, the Foreign Lands Paying Court troupe, wearing brocade jackets, girded with silver girdles, crowned with barbarian caps, holding treasure trays;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, the Foreign Lands Paying Court troupe, in brocade jackets, silver girdles, barbarian caps, bearing treasure trays;

sentences.zh: 九曰兒童解紅隊，衣紫緋繡襦，係銀帶，冠花砌鳳冠，綬帶；

translations.literal: ninth, the Children's Jiehong troupe, wearing purple and scarlet embroidered jackets, girded with silver belts, crowned with flower-inlaid phoenix crowns, with ribbon sashes;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, the Children's Jiehong troupe, in purple and scarlet embroidered jackets, silver belts, flower-inlaid phoenix crowns, and ribbon sashes;

sentences.zh: 十曰射雕回鶻隊，衣盤雕錦襦，係銀舌鞢，射雕盤。

translations.literal: tenth, the Eagle-Shooting Uighur troupe, wearing brocade jackets patterned with circling eagles, girded with silver-trimmed boots, [bearing] eagle-shooting trays.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, the Eagle-Shooting Uighur troupe, in brocade jackets patterned with circling eagles, silver-trimmed boots, and eagle-shooting trays.

sentences.zh: 女弟子隊凡一百五十三人：一曰菩薩蠻隊，衣緋生色窄砌衣，冠卷雲冠；

translations.literal: The female disciples' troupe numbered one hundred fifty-three in all: first, the Bodhisattva Barbarian troupe, wearing scarlet raw-color narrow-inlaid garments, crowned with rolling-cloud crowns;
translations.idiomatic: The female disciples' troupe comprised one hundred fifty-three dancers in all. First, the Bodhisattva Barbarian troupe, in scarlet raw-dye narrow-inlaid garments and rolling-cloud crowns;

sentences.zh: 二曰感化樂隊，衣青羅生色通衣，背梳髻，係綬帶；

translations.literal: second, the Ganhua Le troupe, wearing blue silk raw-color full-length garments, back-combed chignons, girded with ribbon sashes;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Ganhua Le troupe, in blue silk raw-dye full-length garments, back-combed chignons, and ribbon sashes;

sentences.zh: 三曰拋球樂隊，衣四色繡羅寬衫，係銀帶，奉繡球；

translations.literal: third, the Tossing-Ball Le troupe, wearing four-colored embroidered silk wide shirts, girded with silver belts, presenting embroidered balls;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Tossing-Ball Le troupe, in four-colored embroidered silk wide shirts and silver belts, bearing embroidered balls;

sentences.zh: 四曰佳人剪牲丹隊，衣紅生色砌衣，戴金冠，剪牲丹花；

translations.literal: fourth, the Fair Maidens Trimming Peonies troupe, wearing red raw-color inlaid garments, donning gold crowns, trimming peony blossoms;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Fair Maidens Trimming Peonies troupe, in red raw-dye inlaid garments and gold crowns, trimming peony blossoms;

sentences.zh: 五曰拂霓裳隊，衣紅仙砌衣，碧霞帔，戴仙冠，紅繡抹額；

translations.literal: fifth, the Brushing Rainbow Skirts troupe, wearing red immortal-inlaid garments, jade-azure stoles, donning immortal crowns, red embroidered forehead bands;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Brushing Rainbow Skirts troupe, in red immortal-inlaid garments and jade-azure stoles, immortal crowns, and red embroidered forehead bands;

sentences.zh: 六曰采蓮隊，衣紅羅生色綽子，係暈裙，戴雲鬟髻，乘彩船，執蓮花；

translations.literal: sixth, the Gathering Lotus troupe, wearing red silk raw-color petticoats, girded with halo skirts, crowned with cloud-bun chignons, riding painted boats, holding lotus flowers;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the Gathering Lotus troupe, in red silk raw-dye petticoats and halo skirts, cloud-bun chignons, riding painted boats and holding lotus flowers;

sentences.zh: 七曰鳳迎樂隊，衣紅仙砌衣，戴雲鬟鳳髻；

translations.literal: seventh, the Phoenix Welcoming Le troupe, wearing red immortal-inlaid garments, donning cloud-bun phoenix chignons;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, the Phoenix Welcoming Le troupe, in red immortal-inlaid garments and cloud-bun phoenix chignons;

sentences.zh: 八曰菩薩獻香花隊，衣生色窄砌衣，戴寶冠，執香花盤；

translations.literal: eighth, the Bodhisattvas Presenting Incense and Flowers troupe, wearing raw-color narrow-inlaid garments, donning treasure crowns, holding incense-and-flower trays;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, the Bodhisattvas Presenting Incense and Flowers troupe, in raw-dye narrow-inlaid garments and treasure crowns, bearing incense-and-flower trays;

sentences.zh: 九曰彩雲仙隊，衣黃生色道衣，紫霞帔，冠仙冠，執旌節、鶴扇；

translations.literal: ninth, the Colored Cloud Immortals troupe, wearing yellow raw-color Daoist robes, purple-azure stoles, crowned with immortal crowns, holding banners of authority and crane fans;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, the Colored Cloud Immortals troupe, in yellow raw-dye Daoist robes and purple-azure stoles, immortal crowns, bearing banners of authority and crane fans;

sentences.zh: 十曰打球樂隊，衣四色窄繡羅襦，係銀帶，裹順風腳簇花襆頭，執球杖。

translations.literal: tenth, the Ball-Striking Le troupe, wearing four-colored narrow embroidered silk jackets, girded with silver belts, wrapped in downwind clustered-flower turbans, holding ball-sticks.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, the Ball-Striking Le troupe, in four-colored narrow embroidered silk jackets, silver belts, downwind clustered-flower turbans, and ball-sticks.

sentences.zh: 大抵若此，而復從宜變易。

translations.literal: Broadly they were as this, yet again altered as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking the costumes were as described, though they were altered as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 百戲有蹴球、踏蹻、藏擫、雜旋、獅子、弄槍、鈴瓶、茶碗、氈齪、碎劍、踏索、上竿、筋鬥、擎戴、拗腰、透劍門、打彈丸之類。

translations.literal: The hundred entertainments included kickball, stilt-walking, hidden grasp, mixed spinning, lion [dance], spear play, bell bottles, tea bowls, felt treading, sword breaking, rope walking, pole climbing, tumbling, shoulder bearing, waist bending, passing the sword gate, and pellet shooting, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred entertainments included kickball, stilt-walking, hidden-grasp tricks, mixed acrobatics, lion dances, spear play, bell bottles, tea bowls, felt treading, sword breaking, rope walking, pole climbing, tumbling, shoulder bearing, waist bending, passing the sword gate, pellet shooting, and the like.

sentences.zh: （錫慶院宴會，諸王賜食及宰相筵設時賜樂者，第四部充。）〉

translations.literal: (At banquets in the Xiqing Courtyard, when princes were granted food and when chief ministers' banquets were set out and music was granted, the fourth section supplied them.)
translations.idiomatic: (At banquets in the Xiqing Courtyard, when princes were granted food and when music was granted at chief ministers' banquets, the fourth section of the Music Office supplied it.)

sentences.zh: 建隆中，教坊都知李德升作《長春樂曲》；

translations.literal: In the Jianlong era, Music Office director Li Desheng composed the suite "Changchun Lequ";
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianlong era, Music Office director Li Desheng composed the suite "Changchun Lequ";

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，又作《萬歲升平樂曲》。

translations.literal: in the first year of Qiande, he also composed the suite "Wansui Shengping Lequ."
translations.idiomatic: in the first year of Qiande he also composed "Wansui Shengping Lequ."

sentences.zh: 明年，教坊高班都知郭延美又作《紫雲長壽樂》鼓吹曲，以奏禦焉。

translations.literal: The following year, Music Office senior-rank director Guo Yanmei again composed the wind-and-drum suite "Ziyun Changshou Le" to present before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, senior-rank Music Office director Guo Yanmei composed the wind-and-drum suite "Ziyun Changshou Le" and presented it before the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗洞曉音律，前後親製大小曲及因舊曲創新聲者，總三百九十。

translations.literal: Such pieces as "Yuzhou He Huang'en" and "Jiangsheng Wansui Chun" were all composed in the princely residence to recount Taizu's virtues; most of these suites were kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Such pieces as "Yuzhou He Huang'en" and "Jiangsheng Wansui Chun" were composed in the princely residence to celebrate Taizu's virtues; most of these melodies were kept secret.

sentences.zh: 而《平晉普天樂》者，平河東回所製，《萬國朝天樂》者，又明年所製，每宴享常用之。

translations.literal: "Ping Jin Putian Le" was composed upon the return from pacifying Hedong; "Wanguo Chaotian Le" was composed the following year—each was used at every banquet.
translations.idiomatic: "Ping Jin Putian Le" was composed upon the return from pacifying Hedong, and "Wanguo Chaotian Le" the year after; both were staples at every banquet.

sentences.zh: 然帝勤求治道，未嚐自逸，故舉樂有度。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor diligently sought the way of governance and never indulged himself, so music-making was kept within measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor diligently pursued good governance and never indulged in ease, so performances were kept within measure.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，教坊使郭守中求外任，止賜束帛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, Music Office commissioner Guo Shouzhong sought an outside appointment and was granted only silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi, Music Office commissioner Guo Shouzhong sought an outside appointment and received only bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 真宗不喜鄭聲，而或為雜詞，未嚐宣布於外。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong disliked Zheng music, yet when he occasionally composed miscellaneous lyrics he never proclaimed them abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong disliked decadent Zheng music; though he sometimes composed miscellaneous lyrics, he never released them publicly.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，伶官蔚茂多侍大宴，聞雞唱，殿前都虞候崔翰問之曰：“此可被管弦乎？

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, the performer Wei Maoduo often attended great banquets; hearing a cock crow, the Palace Front commander Cui Han asked him, "Could this be set to strings and pipes?
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era the performer Wei Maoduo often attended great banquets. Hearing a cock crow, Palace Front commander Cui Han asked him, "Could this be set for strings and pipes?

sentences.zh: ” 茂多即法其聲，製曲曰《雞叫子》。

translations.literal: " Maoduo at once patterned its sound and composed the suite "Jijiaozi."
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Maoduo immediately took the sound as his model and composed the suite "Jijiaozi."

sentences.zh: 又民間作新聲者甚眾，而教坊不用也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the common people composed new sounds in great number, yet the Music Office did not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the common people composed new sounds in great profusion, but the Music Office did not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 太宗所製曲，乾興以來通用之，凡新奏十七調，總四十八曲：黃鍾、道調、仙呂、中呂、南呂、正宮、小石、歇指、高平、般涉、大石、中呂、仙呂、雙越調，黃鍾羽。

translations.literal: The suites Taizong composed came into general use from the Qianxing era onward; in all seventeen modes were newly submitted, totaling forty-eight melodies: Huangzhong, Daodiao, Xianlü, Zhonglü, Nanlü, Zhenggong, Xiaoshi, Xiezhi, Gaoping, Banshe, Dashi, Zhonglü, Xianlü, Shuang-Yue mode, and Huangzhong yu.

sentences.zh: 其急慢諸曲幾千數。

translations.literal: The fast and slow suites numbered nearly several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fast and slow suites together numbered nearly several thousand.

sentences.zh: 又法曲、《龜茲》、鼓笛三部，凡二十有四曲。

translations.literal: Moreover, the fayue suites, the "Kuche" suite, and the wind-and-drum section together comprised twenty-four melodies.
translations.idiomatic: In addition, fayue suites, the "Kuche" suite, and the wind-and-drum section together comprised twenty-four pieces.

sentences.zh: 仁宗洞曉音律，每禁中度曲，以賜教坊，或命教坊使撰進，凡五十四曲，朝廷多用之，天聖中，帝嚐問輔臣以古今樂之異同，王曾對曰：“古樂祀天地、宗廟、社稷、山川、鬼神，而聽者莫不和悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was thoroughly versed in pitch and mode; he often composed within the forbidden pitch standard to bestow upon the Music Office, or ordered the Music Office commissioner to draft and submit pieces—in all fifty-four suites, widely used at court. In the Tiansheng era the emperor once asked his chief ministers how ancient and modern music differed. Wang Zeng replied, "Ancient music served to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, mountains, rivers, and spirits, and those who heard it were all harmonious and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was thoroughly versed in pitch and mode. He often composed within the forbidden pitch standard and bestowed the pieces upon the Music Office, or ordered the Music Office commissioner to draft and submit them—fifty-four suites in all, widely used at court. In the Tiansheng era the emperor once asked his chief ministers how ancient and modern music differed. Wang Zeng replied, "Ancient music sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, the altars of soil and grain, mountains, rivers, and spirits, and all who heard it were harmonious and pleased.

sentences.zh: 今樂則不然，徒虞人耳目而蕩人心誌。

translations.literal: Present-day music is not so; it merely pleases men's ears and unsettles men's hearts and wills.
translations.idiomatic: Music today is not so—it merely gratifies the ear and unsettles the heart and will.

sentences.zh: 自昔人君流連荒亡者，莫不由此。

translations.literal: From antiquity, every ruler who lingered in dissipation until ruin did so through this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, every ruler who lingered in dissipation until ruin did so through this.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“朕於聲技固未嚐留意，內外宴遊皆勉強耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "As for vocal arts and performance, I have indeed never paid them heed; inner and outer banquets and excursions are all undertaken reluctantly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "As for vocal arts and performance, I have never paid them heed; inner and outer banquets and excursions are all undertaken reluctantly.

sentences.zh: ”張知白曰：“陛下盛德，外人豈知之，願備書時政記。

translations.literal: " Zhang Zhibai said, "Your Majesty's abundant virtue—how could outsiders know it? I beg that it be fully recorded in the Court Diary.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zhibai said, "Your Majesty's abundant virtue—how could outsiders know it? I beg that it be fully recorded in the Court Diary."

sentences.zh: 世號太常為雅樂，而未嚐施於宴享，豈以正聲為不美聽哉！

translations.literal: The age calls the Court of Imperial Sacrifices "elegant music," yet it has never been employed at banquets—is it because correct tones are thought unpleasant to hear!
translations.idiomatic: The age calls the Court of Imperial Sacrifices "elegant music," yet it has never been used at banquets—is correct tone deemed unpleasant to the ear?

sentences.zh: 夫樂者，樂也，其道雖微妙難知，至於奏之而使人悅豫和平，則不待知音而後能也。

translations.literal: Music is joy; though its Way is subtle and hard to know, when it is performed it makes men pleased, at ease, and harmonious—this needs no connoisseur to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Music is joy; though its Way is subtle and hard to know, when performed it makes men pleased, at ease, and harmonious—no connoisseur is needed to perceive that.

sentences.zh: 今太常樂縣鍾、磬、塤、篪、搏拊之器，與夫舞綴羽、籥、幹、戚之製，類皆仿古，逮振作之，則聽者不知為樂而觀者厭焉，古樂豈真若此哉！

translations.literal: Now the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' music sets forth bells, chime-stones, ocarinas, bamboo pipes, and clappers, and the regalia of dance pheasants, feathers, flutes, shields, and axes—all broadly antiquarian; when they are struck up, listeners do not know it as music and spectators are weary of it. Was ancient music truly like this!
translations.idiomatic: Today the Court of Imperial Sacrifices arrays bells, chime-stones, ocarinas, bamboo pipes, and clappers, with dance regalia of pheasant feathers, flutes, shields, and axes—all broadly antiquarian. When they are struck up, listeners do not recognize it as music and spectators grow weary. Was ancient music truly like this?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰“惡鄭聲”，恐其亂雅。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "I hate Zheng music," fearing it would disorder the elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "I hate Zheng music," fearing it would disorder the elegant.

sentences.zh: 亂之雲者，似是而非也。

translations.literal: What is meant by "disorder" is seeming to be what one is not.
translations.idiomatic: By "disorder" he meant seeming to be what one is not.

sentences.zh: 孟子亦曰“今樂猶古樂”，而太常乃與教坊殊絕，何哉？

translations.literal: Mencius also said, "Present music is still like ancient music," yet the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Music Office are utterly separate—why?
translations.idiomatic: Mencius also said, "Present music is still like ancient music," yet the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Music Office stand utterly apart—why?

sentences.zh: 昔李照、胡瑗、阮逸改鑄鍾磬，處士徐復笑之曰：“聖人寓器以聲，不先求其聲而更其器，其可用乎！

translations.literal: In former days Li Zhao, Hu Yuan, and Ruan Yi recast bells and chime-stones; the reclusive gentleman Xu Fu laughed at them, saying, "The sages lodged sound in vessels—they did not first seek the sound and then change the vessels. How could that be used!
translations.idiomatic: In former days Li Zhao, Hu Yuan, and Ruan Yi recast bells and chime-stones. The reclusive gentleman Xu Fu laughed at them, saying, "The sages lodged sound in vessels—they did not first seek the sound and then change the vessels. How could that avail?

sentences.zh: ”照、瑗、逸製作久之，卒無所成。

translations.literal: " Zhao, Yuan, and Yi labored at their manufacture for a long time and ultimately achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao, Yuan, and Yi labored at their manufacture for a long time and ultimately achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 蜀人房庶亦深訂其非是，因著書論古樂與今樂本末不遠，其大略以謂：“上古世質，器與聲樸，後世稍變焉。

translations.literal: The Shu man Fang Shu also deeply criticized their error and therefore wrote a book discussing how ancient and present music in root and branch are not far apart. Its general purport was that in high antiquity the age was plain and instruments and sounds were simple; in later ages they changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu scholar Fang Shu also deeply criticized their error and wrote a book arguing that ancient and present music in root and branch are not far apart. His general purport was that in high antiquity the age was plain and instruments and sounds were simple; in later ages they changed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 金石，鍾磬也，後世易之為方響；

translations.literal: Metal and stone—bells and chime-stones—in later ages were replaced by the fangxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone—bells and chime-stones—in later ages were replaced by the fangxiang;

sentences.zh: 絲竹，琴簫也，後世變之為箏笛。

translations.literal: silk and bamboo—qin and xiao—in later ages were changed to zheng and di.
translations.idiomatic: silk and bamboo—qin and xiao—in later ages gave way to zheng and di.

sentences.zh: 匏，笙也，攢之以鬥；

translations.literal: Gourd—the sheng—was gathered into the dou cluster;
translations.idiomatic: The gourd—the sheng—was gathered into the dou cluster;

sentences.zh: 塤，土也，變而為甌；

translations.literal: clay—the xun—was changed into the ou;
translations.idiomatic: clay—the xun—was changed into the ou;

sentences.zh: 革，麻料也，擊而為鼓；

translations.literal: hide—hemp heads—was struck to make drums;
translations.idiomatic: hide—drumheads—was struck to make drums;

sentences.zh: 木，敔也，貫之為板。

translations.literal: wood—the yu clapper—was strung to make boards.
translations.idiomatic: wood—the yu clapper—was strung to make boards.

sentences.zh: 此八音者，於世甚便，而不達者指廟樂鎛鍾、鎛磬、宮軒為正聲，而概謂夷部、鹵部為淫聲。

translations.literal: These eight kinds of sound are very convenient in the world, yet the uncomprehending point to temple music's great bells, great chime-stones, and palace galleries as correct tone, and broadly call the Yi section and Lu section decadent music.
translations.idiomatic: These eight kinds of sound are very convenient in the world, yet the uncomprehending point to temple music's great bells, great chime-stones, and palace galleries as correct tone, and broadly dismiss the Yi and Lu sections as decadent music.

sentences.zh: 殊不知大輅起於椎輪，龍艘生於落葉，其變則然也。

translations.literal: They do not know that the great carriage arises from the pestle-wheel and the dragon ship from fallen leaves—such is change.
translations.idiomatic: They do not know that the great carriage arises from the pestle-wheel and the dragon ship from fallen leaves—such is change.

sentences.zh: 古者食以俎豆，後世易以杯盂；

translations.literal: In antiquity one ate from zu and dou; in later ages one changed to cups and bowls;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity one ate from zu and dou; in later ages one changed to cups and bowls;

sentences.zh: 簟席以為安，後世更以榻桉。

translations.literal: mats and rush seating were taken for repose; in later ages one changed to couches and low tables.
translations.idiomatic: mats and rush seating served for repose; in later ages one changed to couches and low tables.

sentences.zh: 使聖人復生，不能舍杯盂、榻桉，而復俎豆、簟席之質也。

translations.literal: Were the sages to live again, they could not abandon cups and bowls and couches and low tables to return to the plain quality of zu, dou, mats, and rush seating.
translations.idiomatic: Were the sages to live again, they could not abandon cups and bowls and couches and low tables to return to the plain quality of zu, dou, mats, and rush seating.

sentences.zh: 八音之器，豈異此哉！

translations.literal: Are the instruments of the eight sounds any different from this!
translations.idiomatic: Are the instruments of the eight sounds any different from this?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰‘鄭聲淫’者，豈以其器不若古哉！

translations.literal: When Confucius said "Zheng music is decadent," was it because its instruments were inferior to antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius said "Zheng music is decadent," was it because its instruments were inferior to antiquity?

sentences.zh: 亦疾其聲之變爾。

translations.literal: He also detested the change in its sound.
translations.idiomatic: He detested the change in its sound.

sentences.zh: 試使知樂者，由今之器，寄古之聲，去惉懘靡曼而歸之中和雅正，則感人心、導和氣，不曰治世之音乎！

translations.literal: Suppose one who truly knew music, through present instruments, lodged ancient sounds, removed confused and dissolute strains and returned to central harmony and elegant correctness—then to move men's hearts and guide harmonious qi, would this not be the music of a well-governed age!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose one who truly knew music, through present instruments, lodged ancient sounds, removed confused and dissolute strains and returned to central harmony and elegant correctness—then to move men's hearts and guide harmonious qi, would this not be the music of a well-governed age?

sentences.zh: 然則世所謂雅樂者，未必如古，而教坊所奏，豈盡為淫聲哉！

translations.literal: Then what the age calls elegant music is not necessarily like antiquity, and what the Music Office performs is not all decadent music!
translations.idiomatic: Then what the age calls elegant music is not necessarily like antiquity, and what the Music Office performs is not all decadent music!

sentences.zh: ”當數子紛紛銳意改製之後，庶之論指意獨如此，故存其語，以俟知者。

translations.literal: " When, after those several men had all eagerly pressed reform, Shu's discourse pointed in this direction alone; therefore his words are preserved, to await those who understand.
translations.idiomatic: " When, after those several men had all eagerly pressed reform, Shu's discourse alone pointed in this direction; therefore his words are preserved, to await those who understand.

sentences.zh: 教坊本隸宣徽院，有使、副使、判官、都色長、色長、高班、大小都知。

translations.literal: The Music Office originally was subordinate to the Xuanhui Court, with a commissioner, vice-commissioner, reviewing official, chief color-master, color-master, senior attendants, and senior and junior directors.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office originally was subordinate to the Xuanhui Court, with a commissioner, vice-commissioner, reviewing official, chief color-master, color-master, senior attendants, and senior and junior directors.

sentences.zh: 天聖五年，以內侍二人為鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiansheng, two inner attendants were appointed as controllers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiansheng, two inner attendants were appointed as controllers.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，詔樂工每色額止二人，教頭止三人，有闕即填。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era an edict fixed each instrumental color at only two musicians and teaching heads at only three; vacancies were filled as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era an edict fixed each instrumental color at only two musicians and teaching heads at only three; vacancies were filled as they arose.

sentences.zh: 異時或傳詔增置，許有司論奏。

translations.literal: At other times, if an edict transmitted to increase the complement, the responsible office was permitted to memorialize for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At other times, if an edict transmitted to increase the complement, the responsible office was permitted to memorialize for discussion.

sentences.zh: 使、副歲閱雜劇，把色人分三等，遇三殿應奉人闕，即以次補。

translations.literal: Each year the commissioner and vice-commissioner inspected variety plays; color-holders were divided into three grades; when vacancies occurred among attendants for the Three Halls, they were filled in order.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the commissioner and vice-commissioner inspected variety plays; color-holders were divided into three grades; when vacancies occurred among attendants for the Three Halls, they were filled in order.

sentences.zh: 諸部應奉及二十年、年五十已上，許補廟令或鎮將，官制行，以隸太常寺。

translations.literal: Those who had served in the various sections for twenty years and were fifty years of age or above were permitted to be appointed temple warden or garrison commander; when the official system was implemented, [the Music Office] was placed under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had served in the various sections for twenty years and were fifty or older were permitted appointment as temple warden or garrison commander; when the official system was implemented, the Music Office was placed under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 同天節，寶慈、慶壽宮生辰，皇子、公主生，凡國之慶事，皆進歌樂詞。

translations.literal: On the Tongtian Festival, the birthdays of the Baoci and Qing Shou Palaces, the birth of princes and princesses, and all national celebrations, song lyrics were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tongtian Festival, the birthdays of the Baoci and Qing Shou Palaces, the birth of princes and princesses, and all national celebrations, song lyrics were submitted.

sentences.zh: 熙寧九年，教坊副使花日新言：“樂聲高，歌者難繼。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining, Music Office vice-commissioner Hua Rixin said, "The music sounds high and singers cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xining, Music Office vice-commissioner Hua Rixin said, "The music sounds high and singers cannot follow.

sentences.zh: 方響部器不中度，絲竹從之。

translations.literal: The fangxiang section's instruments are not in pitch; silk and bamboo follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The fangxiang section's instruments are not in pitch; silk and bamboo follow them.

sentences.zh: 宜去噍殺之急，歸嘽緩之易，請下一律，改造方向，以為樂準。

translations.literal: The shrill and cutting urgency should be removed and ease and gentleness restored; I beg that one pitch standard be issued and the fangxiang remade as the musical norm.
translations.idiomatic: The shrill and cutting urgency should be removed and ease and gentleness restored; I beg that one pitch standard be issued and the fangxiang remade as the musical norm.

sentences.zh: 絲竹悉從其聲，則音律諧協，以導中和之氣。

translations.literal: Let silk and bamboo all follow its sound, then pitch and mode will be harmonious and guide the qi of central harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Let silk and bamboo all follow its sound, then pitch and mode will be harmonious and guide the qi of central harmony.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 十一月，奏新樂於化成殿，帝諭近臣曰：“樂聲第降一律，已得寬和之節矣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the new music was performed in the Huacheng Hall; the emperor instructed his close ministers, "The music sound has been lowered one pitch standard and already attained the measure of breadth and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the new music was performed in the Huacheng Hall; the emperor instructed his close ministers, "The music sound has been lowered one pitch standard and already attained the measure of breadth and harmony.

sentences.zh: ”增賜方響為架三十，命太常下法駕、鹵部樂一律，如教坊雲。

translations.literal: " Thirty additional fangxiang frames were bestowed; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to lower the music of the imperial chariot escort and Lu section one pitch standard, as the Music Office said.
translations.idiomatic: " Thirty additional fangxiang frames were bestowed; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to lower the music of the imperial chariot escort and Lu section one pitch standard, as the Music Office had proposed.

sentences.zh: 初，熙寧二年五月，罷宗室正任以上借教坊樂人，至八年，復之，許教樂。

translations.literal: Initially, in the fifth month of the second year of Xining, clansmen of fifth rank and above were forbidden to borrow Music Office musicians; by the eighth year this was restored and teaching music was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the fifth month of the second year of Xining, clansmen of fifth rank and above were forbidden to borrow Music Office musicians; by the eighth year this was restored and teaching music was permitted.

sentences.zh: 政和三年五月，詔：“比以《大晟樂》播之教坊，嘉與天下共之，可以所進樂頒之天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Zhenghe, an edict said, "Recently the Dasheng music has been disseminated to the Music Office; it is fitting that the court share it with all under Heaven—the submitted music may be promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Zhenghe, an edict said, "Recently the Dasheng music has been disseminated to the Music Office; it is fitting that the court share it with all under Heaven—the submitted music may be promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: ”八月，尚書省言：“大晟府宴樂已撥歸教坊，所有諸府從來習學之人，元降指揮令就大晟府教習，今當並就教坊習學。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Ministry of Rites said, "The Dasheng Bureau's banquet music has already been transferred to the Music Office; all persons from the various bureaus who formerly studied it were, by the original directive, ordered to study under the Dasheng Bureau—now they should all study together at the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Ministry of Rites said, "The Dasheng Bureau's banquet music has already been transferred to the Music Office; all persons from the various bureaus who formerly studied it were, by the original directive, ordered to study under the Dasheng Bureau—now they should all study together at the Music Office.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，禮部奏：“教坊樂，春或用商聲，孟或用季律，甚失四時之序。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Ministry of Rites memorialized, "Music Office music—in spring sometimes uses shang mode, in early summer sometimes uses seasonal pitch—it greatly loses the sequence of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Ministry of Rites memorialized, "Music Office music—in spring sometimes uses shang mode, in early summer sometimes uses seasonal pitch—greatly losing the sequence of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 乞以大晟府十二月所定聲律，令教坊閱習，仍令秘書省撰詞。

translations.literal: I beg that the pitch modes the Dasheng Bureau fixed for the twelve months be ordered for Music Office review and practice, and that the Secretariat be ordered to compose lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the pitch modes the Dasheng Bureau fixed for the twelve months be ordered for Music Office review and practice, and that the Secretariat be ordered to compose lyrics."

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎初，省教坊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era of Emperor Gaozong, the Music Office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyan era of Emperor Gaozong, the Music Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 紹興十四年復置，凡樂工四百六十人，以內侍充鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shaoxing it was restored—in all four hundred sixty musicians, with inner attendants serving as controllers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Shaoxing it was restored—in all four hundred sixty musicians, with inner attendants serving as controllers.

sentences.zh: 紹興末復省。

translations.literal: At the end of Shaoxing it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shaoxing it was again abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興二年天申節，將用樂上壽，上曰：“一歲之間，隻兩宮誕日外，餘無所用，不知作何名色。

translations.literal: On the Tian Shen Festival in the second year of Longxing of Emperor Xiaozong, music was to be used for the longevity rite; the emperor said, "Within a year, apart from the two palaces' birthdays, there is otherwise no use for it—I do not know what name to give it.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tian Shen Festival in the second year of Longxing of Emperor Xiaozong, music was to be used for the longevity rite; the emperor said, "Within a year, apart from the two palaces' birthdays, there is otherwise no use for it—I do not know what name to give it.

sentences.zh: ”大臣皆言：“臨時點集，不必置教坊。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers all said, "For temporary assembly there is no need to establish a Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers all said, "For temporary assembly there is no need to establish a Music Office.

sentences.zh: ”上曰：“善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good.

sentences.zh: ”乾道後，北使每歲兩至，亦用樂，但呼市人使之，不置教坊，止令修內司先兩旬教習。

translations.literal: " After the Qiandao era, when northern envoys came twice each year, music was also used, but market people were summoned to perform it; no Music Office was established—only the Directorate of Palace Maintenance was ordered to rehearse them two weeks in advance.
translations.idiomatic: " After the Qiandao era, when northern envoys came twice each year, music was also used, but market people were summoned to perform it; no Music Office was established—only the Directorate of Palace Maintenance was ordered to rehearse them two weeks in advance.

sentences.zh: 舊例用樂人三百人，百戲軍百人，百禽鳴二人，小兒隊七十一人，女童隊百三十七人，築球軍三十二人，起立門行人三十二人，旗鼓四十人，

translations.literal: By former precedent three hundred musicians were used, one hundred men of the Hundred Plays Army, two men for the Hundred Birds' Calls, seventy-one boys' troupe, one hundred thirty-seven girls' troupe, thirty-two cuju kickball troops, thirty-two men of the Standing Gate procession, and forty banners and drums,
translations.idiomatic: By former precedent three hundred musicians were used, one hundred men of the Hundred Plays Army, two men for the Hundred Birds' Calls, seventy-one boys' troupe, one hundred thirty-seven girls' troupe, thirty-two cuju kickball troops, thirty-two men of the Standing Gate procession, and forty banners and drums,

sentences.zh: （以上並臨安府差。）〉

translations.literal: (all above dispatched by the Lin'an prefecture.)
translations.idiomatic: (all above dispatched by the Lin'an prefecture.)

sentences.zh: 相撲等子二十一人。

translations.literal: Twenty-one sumo wrestlers and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one sumo wrestlers and the like.

sentences.zh: （御前忠佐司差。）〉

translations.literal: (dispatched by the Imperial Loyal Retainers Office before the throne.)
translations.idiomatic: (dispatched by the Imperial Loyal Retainers Office before the throne.)

sentences.zh: 命罷小兒及女童隊，餘用之。

translations.literal: An order abolished the boys' and girls' troupes; the remainder were used.
translations.idiomatic: An order abolished the boys' and girls' troupes; the remainder were used.

sentences.zh: 雲韶部者，黃門樂也。

translations.literal: The Yun Shao section is Yellow Gate music.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun Shao section is Yellow Gate music.

sentences.zh: 開寶中平嶺表，擇廣州內臣之聰警者，得八十人，令於教坊習樂藝，賜名簫韶部。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era, when Lingnan was pacified, eighty of the most quick-witted inner attendants of Guangzhou were chosen, ordered to study the musical arts in the Music Office, and granted the name Xiao Shao section.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaibao era, when Lingnan was pacified, eighty of the most quick-witted inner attendants of Guangzhou were chosen, ordered to study music in the Music Office, and granted the name Xiao Shao section.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，改曰雲韶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi it was renamed Yun Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi it was renamed Yun Shao.

sentences.zh: 每上元觀燈，上巳、端午觀水嬉，皆命作樂於宮中。

translations.literal: On each Lantern Festival when lamps are viewed, on the Shangsi and Dragon Boat Festivals when water games are viewed, they were all ordered to perform music within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On each Lantern Festival when lamps are viewed, and on the Shangsi and Dragon Boat Festivals when water games are viewed, they were all ordered to perform music within the palace.

sentences.zh: 遇南至、元正、清明、春秋分社之節，親王內中宴射，則亦用之。

translations.literal: When the winter solstice, New Year's Day, Qingming, and the spring and autumn equinox community festivals arrived, and when imperial princes held archery banquets within the palace, they were also used.
translations.idiomatic: When the winter solstice, New Year's Day, Qingming, and the spring and autumn equinox community festivals arrived, and when imperial princes held archery banquets within the palace, they were also used.

sentences.zh: 奏大曲十三：一曰中呂宮《萬年歡》；

translations.literal: Thirteen grand suites were performed: first, Zhonglü palace "Wannian Huan";
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen grand suites were performed: first, Zhonglü palace, "Wannian Huan";

sentences.zh: 二曰黃鍾宮《中和樂》；

translations.literal: second, Huangzhong palace "Zhonghe Le";
translations.idiomatic: second, Huangzhong palace, "Zhonghe Le";

sentences.zh: 三曰南呂宮《普天獻壽》，此曲亦太宗所製；

translations.literal: third, Nanlü palace "Putian Xian Shou"—this suite was also composed by Taizong;
translations.idiomatic: third, Nanlü palace, "Putian Xian Shou"—this suite was also composed by Taizong;

sentences.zh: 四曰正宮《梁州》；

translations.literal: fourth, Zhenggong "Liangzhou";
translations.idiomatic: fourth, Zhenggong, "Liangzhou";

sentences.zh: 五曰林鍾商《泛清波》；

translations.literal: fifth, Linzhong shang "Fan Qing Bo";
translations.idiomatic: fifth, Linzhong shang, "Fan Qing Bo";

sentences.zh: 六曰雙調《大定樂》；

translations.literal: sixth, Shuang mode "Dading Le";
translations.idiomatic: sixth, Shuang mode, "Dading Le";

sentences.zh: 七曰小石調《喜新春》；

translations.literal: seventh, Xiaoshi mode "Xi Xinchun";
translations.idiomatic: seventh, Xiaoshi mode, "Xi Xinchun";

sentences.zh: 八曰越調《胡渭州》；

translations.literal: eighth, Yue mode "Hu Weizhou";
translations.idiomatic: eighth, Yue mode, "Hu Weizhou";

sentences.zh: 九曰大石調《清平樂》；

translations.literal: ninth, Dashi mode "Qingping Le";
translations.idiomatic: ninth, Dashi mode, "Qingping Le";

sentences.zh: 十曰般涉調《長壽仙》；

translations.literal: tenth, Banshe mode "Changshou Xian";
translations.idiomatic: tenth, Banshe mode, "Changshou Xian";

sentences.zh: 十一曰高平調《罷金鉦》；

translations.literal: eleventh, Gaoping mode "Ba Jin Zheng";
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, Gaoping mode, "Ba Jin Zheng";

sentences.zh: 十二曰中呂調《綠腰》；

translations.literal: twelfth, Zhonglü diao "Lü Yao";
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, Zhonglü diao, "Lü Yao";

sentences.zh: 十三曰仙呂調《采雲歸》。

translations.literal: thirteenth, Xianlü diao "Cai Yun Gui."
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth, Xianlü diao, "Cai Yun Gui."

sentences.zh: 樂用琵琶、箏、笙、觱栗、笛、方響、杖鼓、羯鼓、大鼓、拍板。

translations.literal: The instruments used were pipa, zheng, sheng, bili, di, fangxiang, staff drum, jie drum, great drum, and clappers.
translations.idiomatic: The instruments used were pipa, zheng, sheng, bili, di, fangxiang, staff drum, jie drum, great drum, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 雜劇用傀儡，後不復補。

translations.literal: Variety plays used puppets; afterward they were not replenished.
translations.idiomatic: Variety plays used puppets; afterward they were not replenished.

sentences.zh: 鈞容直，亦軍樂也。

translations.literal: Junrong Direct is also military music.
translations.idiomatic: Junrong Direct is also military music.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，詔籍軍中之善樂者，命曰引龍直。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict registered those skilled in music within the armies and named them Yinlong Direct.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict registered those skilled in music within the armies and named them Yinlong Direct.

sentences.zh: 每巡省遊幸，則騎導車駕而奏樂；

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor toured on inspection, they rode ahead of the imperial carriage and played music;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor toured on inspection, they rode ahead of the imperial carriage and played music;

sentences.zh: 若禦樓觀燈、賜酺，則載第一山車。

translations.literal: if viewing lamps from the imperial tower or granting a grand feast, they were loaded on the First Mountain carriage.
translations.idiomatic: if viewing lamps from the imperial tower or granting a grand feast, they were loaded on the First Mountain carriage.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，又選捧日、天武、拱聖軍曉暢音律者，增多其數，以中使監視，藩臣以樂工上貢者亦隸之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, those from the Sun-Embracing, Heavenly Martial, and Bow-Sage armies who were skilled in pitch and mode were again selected and their number increased, with inner attendants supervising; musicians presented as tribute by frontier lords were also attached.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong, those from the Sun-Embracing, Heavenly Martial, and Bow-Sage armies who were skilled in pitch and mode were again selected and their number increased, with inner attendants supervising; musicians presented as tribute by frontier lords were also attached.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，改名鈞容直，取鈞天之義。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua it was renamed Junrong Direct, taking the meaning of the music of Jun Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua it was renamed Junrong Direct, taking the meaning of the music of Jun Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初用樂工，同雲韶部。

translations.literal: At first musicians were used, as in the Yun Shao section.
translations.idiomatic: At first musicians were used, as in the Yun Shao section.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，因鼓工溫用之請，增《龜茲》部，如教坊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, at drummer Wen Yongzhi's request, the "Kuche" section was added, as in the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, at drummer Wen Yongzhi's request, the "Kuche" section was added, as in the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 其奉天書及四宮觀皆用之。

translations.literal: It was used when presenting the Mandate of Heaven writ and at the Four Palaces' observances.
translations.idiomatic: It was used when presenting the Mandate of Heaven writ and at the Four Palaces' observances.

sentences.zh: 有指揮使一人、都知二人、副都知二人、押班三人、應奉文字一人、監領內侍二人。

translations.literal: There was one commander, two chief directors, two vice chief directors, three ushers, one text attendant, and two supervising inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There was one commander, two chief directors, two vice chief directors, three ushers, one text attendant, and two supervising inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，係籍三百八十三人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou, those on the register numbered three hundred eighty-three persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiayou, those on the register numbered three hundred eighty-three persons.

sentences.zh: 六年，增置四百三十四人，詔以為額，闕即補之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year four hundred thirty-four persons were added; an edict fixed this as the quota; vacancies were filled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year four hundred thirty-four persons were added; an edict fixed this as the quota; vacancies were filled.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔隸班及二十四年、年五十以上者，聽補軍職，隸軍頭司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict permitted those in the roster for twenty-four years and fifty years of age or above to be appointed to military office and attached to the Army Heads Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict permitted those in the roster for twenty-four years and fifty years of age or above to be appointed to military office and attached to the Army Heads Office.

sentences.zh: 其樂舊奏十六調，凡三十六大曲，鼓笛二十一曲，並他曲甚眾。

translations.literal: Its music formerly performed sixteen modes, thirty-six grand suites in all, twenty-one wind-and-drum suites, and very many other melodies besides.
translations.idiomatic: Its music formerly performed sixteen modes, thirty-six grand suites in all, twenty-one wind-and-drum suites, and very many other melodies besides.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，監領內侍言，鈞容直與教坊樂並奏，聲不諧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou the supervising inner attendants said that when Junrong Direct and Music Office music were performed together the sounds were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiayou the supervising inner attendants said that when Junrong Direct and Music Office music were performed together the sounds were not harmonious.

sentences.zh: 詔罷鈞容舊十六調，取教坊十七調肄習之，雖間有損益，然其大曲、曲破並急、慢諸曲，與教坊頗同矣。

translations.literal: An edict abolished Junrong's former sixteen modes; the Music Office's seventeen modes were taken for practice; though there were occasional additions and subtractions, its grand suites, suite breakdowns, and fast and slow suites were largely the same as the Music Office's.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished Junrong's former sixteen modes; the Music Office's seventeen modes were taken for practice; though there were occasional additions and subtractions, its grand suites, suite breakdowns, and fast and slow suites were largely the same as the Music Office's.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，鈞容直舊管四百人，楊存中請復收補，權以舊管之半為額，尋聞其召募騷擾，降詔止之。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era Junrong Direct formerly managed four hundred persons; Yang Cunzhong requested restoration and recruitment, temporarily fixing the quota at half the former complement; soon it was heard that recruitment caused disturbance, and an edict halted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaoxing era Junrong Direct formerly managed four hundred persons; Yang Cunzhong requested restoration and recruitment, temporarily fixing the quota at half the former complement; soon it was heard that recruitment caused disturbance, and an edict halted it.

sentences.zh: 及其以應奉有勞，進呈推賞，又申諭止於支賜一次，庶杜其日後希望。

translations.literal: When he was advanced and rewarded for meritorious attendance, the emperor again instructed that rewards be limited to a single grant of valuables, to block their hopes thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: When he was advanced and rewarded for meritorious attendance, the emperor again instructed that rewards be limited to a single grant of valuables, to block their hopes thereafter.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年，復詔鈞容班可蠲省，令殿司比擬一等班直收頓，內老弱癃疾者放停。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing an edict again permitted reduction of the Junrong roster; the Palace Service was ordered to compare and absorb them into a first-grade roster guard, dismissing the old and weak and infirm.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing an edict again permitted reduction of the Junrong roster; the Palace Service was ordered to compare and absorb them into a first-grade roster guard, dismissing the old and weak and infirm.

sentences.zh: 教坊所嚐援祖宗舊典，點選入教，雖暫從其請，紹興三十一年有詔，教坊即日蠲罷，各令自便。

translations.literal: The Music Office often cited the ancestral statutes and selected persons for entry into teaching; though they temporarily assented to the request, in the thirty-first year of Shaoxing there was an edict abolishing the Music Office that very day, each man released to go as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office often cited the ancestral statutes and selected persons for entry into teaching; though they temporarily assented to the request, in the thirty-first year of Shaoxing there was an edict abolishing the Music Office that very day, each man released to go as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 東西班樂，亦太平興國中選東西班習樂者，樂器獨用銀字觱栗、小笛、小笙。

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western Ban music was also chosen in the Taiping Xingguo era from those in the Eastern and Western Bans who studied music; the instruments used exclusively were silver-letter bili, small di, and small sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern and Western Ban music was also chosen in the Taiping Xingguo era from those in the Eastern and Western Bans who studied music; the instruments used exclusively were silver-letter bili, small di, and small sheng.

sentences.zh: 每騎從車駕而奏樂，或巡方則夜奏於行宮殿庭。

translations.literal: Whenever they followed the imperial carriage and played music, or when the emperor toured the regions they played at night in the traveling palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they followed the imperial carriage and played music, or when the emperor toured the regions they played at night in the traveling palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 諸軍皆有善樂者，每車駕親祀回，則衣緋綠衣，自青城至朱雀門，列於禦道之左右，奏樂迎奉，其聲相屬，聞十數里。

translations.literal: Every army had those skilled in music; whenever the emperor personally sacrificed and returned, they wore scarlet and green garments from Qingcheng to the Vermilion Bird Gate, arrayed along both sides of the imperial way, performing music in welcome—one sound succeeding another, heard for ten-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: Every army had those skilled in music; whenever the emperor personally sacrificed and returned, they wore scarlet and green garments from Qingcheng to the Vermilion Bird Gate, arrayed along both sides of the imperial way, performing music in welcome—one sound succeeding another, heard for ten-odd li.

sentences.zh: 或軍宴設亦奏之。

translations.literal: They also performed at army banquets.
translations.idiomatic: They also performed at army banquets.

sentences.zh: 棹刀槍牌翻歌等，不常置。

translations.literal: Pole-saber, spear-shield, and banner-flipping songs and the like were not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Pole-saber, spear-shield, and banner-flipping songs and the like were not regularly established.

sentences.zh: 清衛軍習樂者，令鈞容直教之，內侍主其事，園苑賜會及館待契丹使人。

translations.literal: Those in the Clear Guard Army who studied music were ordered taught by Junrong Direct, with inner attendants presiding; they were used at garden-park grants of banquets and when hosting Khitan envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the Clear Guard Army who studied music were ordered taught by Junrong Direct, with inner attendants presiding; they were used at garden-park grants of banquets and when hosting Khitan envoys.

sentences.zh: 又有親從親事樂及開封府衙前樂，園苑又分用諸軍樂，諸州皆有衙前樂。

translations.literal: There were also music of the Personal Retinue and Personal Affairs, and music before the Kaifeng prefectural yamen; the garden parks also separately employed various army music, and every prefecture had yamen-front music.
translations.idiomatic: There were also music of the Personal Retinue and Personal Affairs, and music before the Kaifeng prefectural yamen; the garden parks also separately employed various army music, and every prefecture had yamen-front music.

sentences.zh: 四夷樂者，元豐六年五月，召見米脂砦所降戎樂四十二人，奏樂於崇政殿，以三班借職王恩等六人差監在京閑慢庫務門及舊城門敢勇三十六人，與茶酒新任殿侍。

translations.literal: Barbarian music: in the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng, forty-two surrendered Rong musicians from the Mizhi stockade were summoned and performed in the Chongzheng Hall; six men on provisional Third-Rank assignment, Wang En and others, were differenced to supervise the idle and slow capital storehouse gates and the old city gate Dare-to-Win corps of thirty-six men, together with tea-and-wine newly appointed palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian music: in the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng, forty-two surrendered Rong musicians from the Mizhi stockade were summoned and performed in the Chongzheng Hall; six men on provisional Third-Rank assignment, Wang En and others, were differenced to supervise the idle and slow capital storehouse gates and the old city gate Dare-to-Win corps of thirty-six men, together with tea-and-wine newly appointed palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 《大晟樂書》曰：“前此宮架之外，列熊羆案，所奏皆夷樂也，豈容淆雜大樂！

translations.literal: The Book of Dasheng Music says, "Before this, beyond the palace frame, the Bear and Pi table was arrayed and what was performed was all barbarian music—how could it be mixed with great music!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Dasheng Music says, "Before this, beyond the palace frame, the Bear and Pi table was arrayed and what was performed was all barbarian music—how could it be mixed with great music!

sentences.zh: 乃奏罷之。

translations.literal: Therefore it was memorialized and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it was memorialized and abolished.

sentences.zh: 然古鞮鞻氏掌四夷樂，靺師、旄人各有所掌，以承祭祀，以供宴享。

translations.literal: Yet in antiquity the Di and Li clans managed the four barbarians' music; the Mo masters and Mao men each had their charge, to undertake sacrifice and supply banquet enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in antiquity the Di and Li clans managed the four barbarians' music; the Mo masters and Mao men each had their charge, to undertake sacrifice and supply banquet enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 蓋中天下而立，得四海之歡心，使鼓舞焉，先王之所不廢也。

translations.literal: For one who stands at the center of all under Heaven and wins the hearts of the four seas, to make them drum and dance—this the former kings did not abolish.
translations.idiomatic: For one who stands at the center of all under Heaven and wins the hearts of the four seas, to make them drum and dance—this the former kings did not abolish.

sentences.zh: 《漢律》曰：‘每大朝會宜設於殿門之外。

translations.literal: The Han Code says, "At each great court assembly they should be set outside the hall doors.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Code says, "At each great court assembly they should be set outside the hall doors.

sentences.zh: ’天子禦樓，則宮架之外列於道側，豈可旋於廣庭，與大樂並奏哉！

translations.literal: " When the Son of Heaven mounts the tower, they are arrayed outside the palace frame along the roadside—how could they be turned about in the broad courtyard and performed together with great music!
translations.idiomatic: " When the Son of Heaven mounts the tower, they are arrayed outside the palace frame along the roadside—how could they be turned about in the broad courtyard and performed together with great music!
